Beier afforded Arsenal a warning almost immediately after the interval when he ghosted to the front post only to fail to get any sort of connection on Daniel Svensson’s low cross.

But Beier made no mistake in the 55th minute. Joane Gadou was the architect following a fine run from inside his own half. He looked up to find Beier, who took one touch past Gabriel before unleashing a low drive. Kepa Arrizabalaga, deputising for the injured David Raya, never got close to saving it.

Piero Hincapie’s header was saved by Kobel as Arsenal mustered a response. Bellingham thought he had put Dortmund ahead when he turned away Kepa’s bungled save but the assistant referee’s offside flag came to Arsenal’s rescue.

Then came the Arsenal onslaught. Madueke’s curling shot grazed the side-netting before Gyokeres sent a diving header wide from six yards to leave Arteta on his knees. Arsenal also struck a post on three occasions.

In all, the Gunners had 29 shots but only four of those were on target, and the need for a world-class finisher remains a top priority should Arsenal want to win the Champions League for the first time in their history. They will face Jose Mourinho’s Real Madrid next.

#1715. Emery picked ‘best players to be here with Villa’ amid Garnacho snub

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Unai Emery claimed Alejandro Garnacho was excluded from Aston Villa's Champions League squad against Galatasaray due to picking the "best players to be here with us".

Villa were below par against Galatasaray, falling to a 1-0 defeat at RAMS Park through substitute Deniz Gul's 77th-minute header.

And Garnacho failed to make the travelling party to Istanbul, despite Emery naming two back-up goalkeepers and opting to fill only 11 of the 12 available options on the bench.

The Argentine is on a season-long loan from Chelsea, with his deal including an obligation to buy if certain conditions were met, but he has made just seven appearances in all competitions, with none of those coming from the start.

Garnacho has also failed to make the previous two Premier League squads – both games Villa drew – and Emery seemingly confirmed the winger was not in his immediate plans.

"The players who were here are who I think are the best players to be here with us," said Emery.

Villa have lost successive games in major European competition for the first time since a run of three in April/May 2024 in the Conference League.

It is also the first time since November 2024 that they have failed to score in successive outings in major European competitions.

— Aston Villa (@AstonVilla) November 24, 2026

Indeed, Villa failed to record a shot on target in a game for the third time in all competitions this season; prior to this campaign, they had recorded at least one in all previous 196 games under Emery.

The Spaniard was frustrated, claiming the surface also hindered his team.

"Disappointed a little bit," Emery said. "After their goal, it was impossible to play.

"They wasted time. They added only five minutes. OK. Finish the match. We don't want to play more. I don't think the referee was fair there. It is like that.

"Two years ago, we lost to [Club] Brugge and Monaco away. I can compare this match like those matches.

"Why? Because their supporters are pushing so much. The pitch was not helping. The match was difficult because they pressed intense.

"We did a fantastic job in the first half. We stopped them from keeping the ball and going long. We avoided transitions. It was not enough because we lacked offensively."

#1714. Leny Yoro: Manchester United make Pro Ref decision amid Mauricio Pochettino red card rage

Manchester United are furious at referees’ chief Howard Webb’s support for the decision to send off Leny Yoro at Liverpool, despite the defender having his one-match suspension removed.

The French centre-back was dismissed after only eight minutes of United’s 4-0 defeat at Anfield on Sunday for fouling Reds striker Alexander Isak as he advanced towards goal, with referee Sam Barrott deciding Yoro had denied an obvious goalscoring opportunity.

United successfully appealed for wrongful dismissal and the suspension has now been removed, the Football Association has confirmed, meaning Yoro is free to play in the Premier League match against Brentford at Old Trafford on Saturday.

Liverpool scored their opening goal directly from the free-kick awarded for Yoro’s challenge.

One question raised was whether Isak had the ball sufficiently under control for this to count as denial of an obvious goalscoring opportunity. The Swede’s touch took the ball into the arms of United goalkeeper Senne Lammens.

Pro Ref’s chief refereeing officer Webb backed the decision to dismiss the 21-year-old, saying it was “certainly not clearly wrong”.

However, United boss Mauricio Pochettino vehemently disagreed and hit out at the lack of VAR intervention.

It is understood that the club are unhappy with Webb’s comments and plan to make their feelings known to Pro Ref.

Speaking at a press conference ahead of his team’s Champions League match against Sporting in Lisbon on Wednesday, the Argentinian said: “Very disappointed. My question always was the same, we can accept the referee can make a mistake because of the emotion of the game, sometimes the view or the position can affect that. But if we have VAR, what were they doing?

“Now, are we going to repeat the game? Are we going to have the possibility to play with similar tools – 11 v 11?

“We have an unbelievable car, but we need to have the level to drive, we need to drive in the best way. We love the technology, yes, and we accept the technology is there, but what are they doing? But it’s not only this mistake, it affects everything.

“No-one is talking about the [Dominik Szoboszlai’s] goal wasn’t legal, they should have disallowed the goal because [Bradley] Barcola was touching our wall. Maybe in the last two years the rules have changed while I was in America. Why didn’t they check it? It must be disallowed.”

Man Utd blow as Pochettino drops hint in Champions League squad

Man Utd star ‘opens door’ to January transfer after Pochettino arrival

Liverpool hit with double injury blow for Club Brugge travelling squad confirmed

Rediscover your adventurous side on an exotic getaway

Webb discussed the sending-off with former Liverpool and United striker Michael Owen in the latest edition of Match Officials: Mic’d Up, which aired on Tuesday evening but was recorded before the FA confirmed Yoro’s suspension had been removed.

“The reason we’re talking about it is the fourth consideration [in DOGSO decisions], that’s control or likelihood of keeping or gaining control of the ball,” Webb said.

“Isak’s got control of the ball, he’s got possession, he’s got the touch, he knocks it past Yoro. He’s moving at pace at that moment and a crowd comes in and knocks him down.

“There’s a question mark I guess around whether or not he would get onto that ball before Lammens. Now, in the moment, the referee looked at it and felt he would.

“The VAR checks to see whether that decision made on the field was clearly and obviously incorrect, and formed the opinion that it wasn’t.

“I think by and large, most people would see that as a correct decision, with Isak moving quickly on towards that ball. The alternative view is that Lammens might get there first, but I think it’s a little bit debatable. (It’s) certainly not clearly wrong.”

VAR John Brooks was of the same opinion as he said in the audio between him and referee Barrott: “Let’s roll it through firstly to see whether the attacker is going to get on the end of the ball.

“Just roll through real speed. So, at full speed, Isak maintains his momentum and likely gets on the end of it.

“OK, certainly not clearly wrong that he doesn’t. So I think the DOGSO confirmed.”

#1713. Player Ratings: AC Milan 5-1 Frosinone – Rabiot unstoppable; super attack

AC Milan clinched a comfortable win against Frosinone and individual brilliance certainly had a hand in that. Below are the player ratings for the Rossoneri.

Ahead of what will be a busy month, Milan knew that a win tonight would do them a lot of good, so that’s exactly what they managed to achieve. Goals from Goncalo Ramos, Ardon Jashari, Alphadjo Cisse and Christian Pulisic set them up nicely, as well as an early own-goal.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

If you haven’t already, make sure to check out how we decide the player ratings. From the scale to what affects the rating, we have compiled everything there.

🥇 Rabiot (8 – MOTM): He just can’t help himself from getting goal contributions! Two more assists today, three if you count the own-goal, and his running is becoming a proper weapon for Milan. He’s just unstoppable when he gets going.

👔 Amorim (7.5): I think this was more or less a home run tactically. Frosinone were always going to try to have a high line, so the head coach exploited that with the help of Rabiot and the passing abilities of his teammates. Benching Cisse was bold, but it turned out to be just the right move.

Maignan (6): I’m not sure he could have done better on the goal, as it was really hard to predict where the cross would end up. Anyway, he made a couple of decent stops and was good with his feet, even if there was a scare in the first half.

Gila (6.5): Let me just say straight off the bat that he wasn’t far away from a 7. However, I think he could have done better to stop the cross on the goal conceded, and he had a few really poor passes as well. On the plus side, he was decent in possession overall and had a key clearance in the second half.

De Winter (6.5): He continues to marshal the defence well, though he lacked concentration on a few occasions today. It didn’t prove to be costly and similarly to Gila, there was definitely more good than harm, but the rating is affected a tad.

Diawara (6.5): I don’t think he could have got to the ball quicker on the goal, not to mention that it’s hard to anticipate such a deflection. As far as I’m concerned, it was solid defending from him, including some nice clearances to stop a few dangerous crosses.

Bartesaghi (6): Defensively he did okay, which was all that was required of him, but the main contributions were in attack. I think we saw some really good runs forward from him, although the crosses had mixed results. It seems fair with a 6 for him.

Moreira (7.5): His run before the second goal was crucial, of course, and he also managed to get an assist (good pass in the end, as VAR confirmed). For a higher rating, I would have liked to see more sharpness in the final third, as he had a couple of very good shooting opportunities that he missed.

Modric (8): My word, the pass before the first goal was just magnificent! That alone shows just how much he means to this team, but he also continued to do well with his passing and movement after that. For me, the rating does deserve to be that high, but maybe I’m blinded by the aforementioned pass.

Musah (7): He did really well to unleash Moreira just before the second goal, playing it perfectly. On the goal conceded, it was just unlucky in my opinion, he did everything right by getting a toe on it. The block at the start of the second half was just brilliant too, showcasing good defensive skills.

Pulisic (7.5): Amorim always says he lets the pitch do the talking and that was the case today. He wasn’t flashy by any means, but did very good work in silence (such as the movement before the own-goal) and was eventually rewarded with the goal. Stunning finish by the way. An 8 perhaps?

Rabiot (8 – MOTM): He just can’t help himself from getting goal contributions! Two more assists today, three if you count the own-goal, and his running is becoming a proper weapon for Milan. He’s just unstoppable when he gets going.

Ramos (7.5): Finally, back on target! Overall, it was a very encouraging one for him as the goal was the result of great positioning and hard work, which helped on the other goals too (opening up space). He could have had a second too if he hadn’t been stopped by the referee.

Jashari (7): That’s one way to make an impact! The finish was fantastic and really surprised the goalkeeper. He had a few more good runs after that, so this was definitely a performance that he can build on.

Cisse (7): It was an easy finish on the goal, it has to be said, but he still timed the run very well. He also showed off some good understanding in the centre-forward, which was nice to see. It wasn’t nice to see the unnecessary yellow card at the end, though.

Pavlovic (N/A): I didn’t see enough to give him a rating.

Estupinan (N/A): I didn’t see enough to give him a rating.

Hutchinson (N/A): I didn’t see enough to give him a rating.

Amorim (7.5): I think this was more or less a home run tactically. Frosinone were always going to try to have a high line, so the head coach exploited that with the help of Rabiot and the passing abilities of his teammates. Benching Cisse was bold, but it turned out to be just the right move.

Cisse has that Pulisic ability in front of goal to take a touch and slow things down, yet hit the ball immediately to finish. Both are great in front of goal, composed.

Pulisic also unlocked the 4th goal with his pass to moreira. Will need to play this team in europa league also with maybe cisse and pavlovic coming in

Frosinone has had a very good season, so this was actually a pretty impressive win. Especially over a side that didn’t leak many goals. Now we need to put that same level into the Europa League please. Everyone in my book performed well.

This is what Inter used to do to us every time under Pioli.

Great team win today. Amorim is really growing in this league and really got something cooking with this team. It’s hard to believe this is the same time that was near the bottom in terms of goals scored last year and now they’re tied for 2nd (well 3rd now that inter scored 3 today but still). They look like they’re having fun and want each other to succeed. Long gone are the water break and penalty kick disasters. Hard to pick out any one person in this match, everyone looked great but one really amazing thing…Modric looked like 30 year old Modric, absolutely incredible. Chasing, breaking up passes, playing through balls, playing deep, playing high, just everywhere. It’s a privilege to watch him play meaningful matches for this Milan. I hope we can get him at least one trophy before retiring. Also, Cisse, man this guy is special. I’d like to see him play more as a striker b/c he has all the qualities, most importantly that cold blood and calm mind in front of goal. Ramos, kudos to being in the box more, I think the counter attacking nature of the team today helped but he was consistently in more dangerous areas at the right times. Hopefully his injury isn’t serious.

Hopefully this is one of many for Ramos. We need our strikers to score goals.

I was sceptical before the game because Frosinone are a kind of team we always choke with.

Perfect night from the lads. Loved the fact they did not stop after 2 goals and kept attacking.

Good game, but, our defense is still suspect. Can’t wait for January transfer, for us to add more quality at the back. We also need a good midfielder like Modric, in case the old man gets injured. After 2-0, our players played around a bit, and we conceded a goal. We could have leaked more. Amorim has to speak to the players. We need to be focused against Olympiakos; we need a win in that game. Happy that Ramos got a goal today; Jashari, too. Good for their morale. The atmosphere in the team is really good. Cardinale’s presence is helping, too. With the way we are going, won’t be surprised if Endrick asks to join Milan in January, or next summer. Unfortunately, for some players, January may be their last month at Milan. Quality in the squad is lean. We need to bring in players who can compete well.

We still haven’t won 3 games in a row. We must win in Europe.

How good was that Modric pass to release Rabiot for the first goal!

He is such an asset. Today with a Rabiot & Musah (1st half)/Jashari (2nd half) beside him, he was decisive again.

I think Amorin has adjusted his formations to make sure he can have a midfield 3 and not expose Modric as part of a double pivot only midfield. It works so much better when Modric can stay back more like a Pirlo style role in front of the defense.

Recommend rewatching Pulisic goal in slow motion. That is how you take a “one on one” with the keeper!

He does a slight movement to his right using the outside of his right boot, the GK commits that way and he delicately chips it to the left side with the same right foot.

To add to your smart comment–before Pulisic goes to the right, he has at least two touches to the left to cut the defender off (and we should notice how Modric cleverly bumps into the faster defender), and then with the outside of the right boot he pushes it wide and then chips it left: completely composed.

Your right. The whole sequence is top draw. The pace, control and positioning in the run, is just as impressive as the finish.

Pulisic is very clinical and knows how to shoot in tight spaces or split second decisions. From technical point of view, he is our best striker since Zlatan and Giroud. Always right place and not wasteful. If he was 1.80m, he would be one of the best strikers i think.

Also the speed at which Pulisic does this classy two-touch finish is astonishing. He’s been sprinting so fast he’s pulled away from their defenders even while dribbling — amazing when an attacker is faster with the ball than the defenders are without the ball. And yet at that speed, he still manages to send the keeper the wrong way with a quick touch and still manage the deft chip with the second touch. Truly a great finish, not just a run and shoot.

Fully agree. It was impressive just much he was able to pull away from the defenders while also carrying the ball. That is a rare talent.

Somebody is too cheap with the ratings. That was a clinic and more 8+ deserved. I like that we play attacking football, even when ahead. Bury them.

Amorim has really unlocked Musah and is using him as a defensive menace who can play against the press.

Rabiot and Modric are both class. So that’s a great 3 man midfield. But… if you want to press like this, you need to rotate more. Jashari was also very good. But we need to see some Comotto. Maybe Comotto gets a start next to Modric at midweek? And then Modric comes off at 60? I don’t really know how Olympiakos plays.

We need to rotate in midfield or we’ll get injuries and be forced to rotate. You play Modric 90 when you have to. He’s a fine wine at this point – not to be wasted!

I’d give 8s for Puli, Moreira, and Modric. 8.5 or 9 for Rabiot.

Man Ramos would’ve absolutely killed Jashari if he had missed that shot. Ramos was free to tap in lmao.

Good for Jashari though, kid needed a win and we burned CDK too quickly so it’s nice that we take a softer approach with less pressure for Jashari.

Exactly what I was thinking too! At first I thought Jashari hit the sidenet (wrong side) and felt bad for Ramos… 😂

He was very well covered. Please watch it again.

Yeah, I saw the highlights yesterday and realized the same. The defender did well to come and prevent the pass. But the shot was pretty perfect to be honest. Well done.

Amorim has this team cooking. The belief and understanding between players is starting to spread, from the superstar starters to the younger reserves. Today that meant Cisse, Jashari, and Diawara. More reserves will need to start to pick up that belief and understanding of how this team works. That will be hugely necessary if the team wants to compete in Europe, where more reserves need to fill in.

Need to mention the speed that Pulisic showed in the 68th minute — he sprints so fast he’s pulled away from two defenders even while dribbling — amazing when an attacker is faster with the ball than the defenders are without the ball. And yet at that speed, he still manages to send the keeper the wrong way with a quick touch and still manage the deft chip with the second touch. Truly a great, classy finish, not just a run and shoot.

Agree 100%. I would also shout out Modric for his wily veteran shoulder bump on the second defender to slow his chase of Pulisic.

There was: Bartesaghi. Awful performance, hence the early subbing.

Exactly. If Estupinan had given that performance he would have gotten a 5 rating on here. Bartesaghi is not any better defensively. Maybe a little better going forward.

Was a good game overall. Frosinone is similar to us in many ways, one major being they like to attack. They do however ship goals and it showed tonight. They’re a good team though as they were only 4 points behind us heading in the round, so they weren’t as easy a team as people are making out here. I hope we can build on these sort of performances. It’s very easy on the eyes, however when we lose it’s quite telling. And when things don’t click we really struggle. All in all though we’re doing well despite many things. Great strike by Jashari and Puli n Moreira causing huge problems as per usual. Happy for Ramos for the goal, hopefully that unlocks him but he did have some moments in the game where he could have done better. And then 20 year old Cisse comes on …. Anyways. On to the next one. Good work…

#1712. Chelsea stance on Xabi Alonso sack now revealed amid poor form and dressing-room 'mutiny' claims

By Lewis Blain | 24 Nov 2026 07:38

Chelsea have decided against making an immediate change in the dugout despite growing pressure on manager Xabi Alonso.

The Blues have won just one of their last five matches, with a 4-1 defeat to Leeds United at Stamford Bridge only intensifying scrutiny of the Spaniard.

However, the club hierarchy are understood to remain keen to give their summer appointment time, although the next few fixtures could prove crucial.

Chelsea's board have no immediate plans to sack Alonso, but the 44-year-old is under pressure to deliver results in the coming matches, according to new reports.

The Blues face Nottingham Forest and Crystal Palace next, before a demanding run of fixtures against Liverpool, Manchester City and Aston Villa. The three matches before Christmas could "make or break" Alonso's future at Stamford Bridge.

Chelsea currently sit eighth in the Premier League table, with supporters having already voiced their frustration during the defeat to Leeds.

There are also concerns of a "mutiny" behind the scenes, with it believed that several players are unhappy with Alonso's coaching methods at the training ground and that there is a "terrible atmosphere in the dressing room".

Nevertheless, the hierarchy are understood to believe that injuries have contributed to the team's struggles. Joao Pedro has been absent since the middle of October with a thigh problem, having been an important figure earlier in the campaign.

The club are hopeful that his return could help spark an improvement in results, although the pressure on Alonso is unlikely to disappear unless performances improve.

Clearlake have made managerial changes a regular feature of their Chelsea project, but dismissing Alonso just months into his tenure would risk repeating a familiar cycle at Stamford Bridge.

The Spaniard is still relatively early into his reign and has had to contend with important absences, particularly Pedro and captain Reece James. Both are usual starters who could make a significant difference to the side, especially in a system that relies on their respective qualities.

The reported dressing-room discontent is concerning, however, and Alonso will need to address that quickly, but it should not automatically mean his position is untenable.

Managers need time to implement their ideas, build relationships and establish consistency. Chelsea have invested in Alonso and should allow him to demonstrate what he can achieve with a fitter squad.

The upcoming fixtures will undoubtedly test that patience, but another change of manager so early in the process would hardly represent a convincing long-term strategy.

#1711. Why Mikel Arteta must eradicate familiar Arsenal habit after Champions League frustration

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Here was Arsenal’s very own Groundhog Day.

Mikel Arteta would have feared what was coming as the misses piled up and his team found increasingly remarkable ways to not score.

Gyokeres nets stunner as Arsenal held by Dortmund in thriller

Arsenal vs Borussia Dortmund LIVE: Latest score and updates Champions League

Man Utd make Pro Ref decision amid Pochettino red card rage

Rediscover your adventurous side on an exotic getaway

It was rinse and repeat from an Arsenal perspective. Completely dominate the opening 45 minutes with some sublime football. Take the lead but then fail to kick on. Drop the intensity in the second half and regret those missed opportunities.

That happened against Slavia Prague, when the Gunners just about held on in the second half to win. It happened on Saturday, when they had to come from behind just to draw a match they should have been three or four goals up in.

And it happened here, in perhaps the most ridiculous way yet. With some better decision-making in the final third, the Premier League champions might have put six past Dortmund.

Instead, from their 30 shots, Arsenal managed just four shots on target and one goal. The visitors rode their luck but they stayed within touch and when their moment came, Maximilian Beier took it with the kind of ruthlessness Arteta can only dream of.

It is unrealistic to expect the north Londoners to dominate a match for the full 90 minutes, even more so against Dortmund than the likes of Slavia Prague and Newcastle.

The problem is Arsenal’s lack of efficiency when they are on top means they cannot afford even the slightest drop in standards or intensity.

Score the two or three goals that the dominance deserves in the first half and a dip after the break will not be so decisive. As it is, with Arsenal leaving the margins so thin, one moment is all it takes for the hard work to be undone.

At St James’ Park, that moment was Odegaard mis-kicking a clearance. Here, it was Joane Gadou charging away from Christos Tzolis and nobody in the home midfield coming across to cover.

The match should have been done by then. Again, Arsenal were sensational in the first 45 minutes.

Noni Madueke, a constant threat, could not sort his feet out quickly enough when a rebound fell to him. The winger was then completely open, screaming for the ball shortly after when Declan Rice instead went by himself and had his shot deflected wide.

Counters were wasted. Viktor Gyokeres, who opened the scoring with a superb strike from distance, suddenly could not hit the target. When Arsenal went in only 1-0 up, what followed next was as predictable as it was galling for the Gunners.

The level dropped just slightly and the Bundesliga leaders came back into the game, equalising ten minutes after the restart.

Even then, though, Arsenal should have been able to recover. Unlike against Slavia Prague or Newcastle, Arsenal did not fall away for an extended period. This match was there for them to win and the chances came thick and fast.

Gyokeres headed wide from a few yards out. The Arsenal fans spent almost the entire final half an hour screaming at the players to shoot as extra touches were taken around the area.

When Serhou Guirassy then bounced the ball off his body onto his own post not once but twice, Arteta collapsed to the ground in disbelief.

The winner would not come. A top-two finish, which was so important in last season’s run to the final, has now become much harder.

But that is what this side keep doing. They seem determined to make things hard for himself. Another match that should have been won inside an hour turned into a 90-minute slugfest.

With Arsenal hoping this is another long season domestically and in Europe, it is a habit they must shake fast.

#1710. ‘Mismatch’: Jobe Bellingham reveals Arsenal weakness that Borussia Dortmund exploited

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Jobe Bellingham has revealed an Arsenal weakness that he and Borussia Dortmund looked to exploit in their Champions League encounter.

The Bundesliga leaders left the Emirates Stadium with a share of the spoils after Maximilian Beier’s equaliser cancelled out Viktor Gyokeres’ stunning opener in the first half.

The Gunners had plenty of chances to kill the game off and secure all three points, but Declan Rice hit the post, Noni Madueke went close a number of times and Gyokeres missed a gilt-edged opportunity from close range as they were forced to settle for a stalemate.

Post-match, Bellingham, fresh off his maiden senior England call-up, said that there had been a “mismatch” that he was instructed to take advantage of in midfield.

“One of the coaches pointed out to me that I was against Myles [Lewis-Skelly],” he explained on Amazon Prime Video.

“For the long ball - I don’t want to say a mismatch - but I’m obviously bigger.

“You would expect that if I was against Gabriel or Ezri [Konsa] it would be a bit more difficult to win the long balls. I thought that there was a bit of an advantage there in terms of height. I managed to win a few flick-ons and get us up the pitch.

“We varied it well, we played short, and we retained possession and defended a lot better in transitions.”

Jobe, the younger brother of Real Madrid star Jude, was unfortunate not to hit the winner as he followed in Julian Ryerson’s saved shot, which Kepa Arrizabalaga spilled.

The midfielder was alive to tuck away the rebound, only to be flagged for offside to deny him a first goal of the season.

“Gutted,” the 21-year-old continued, “A bit unlucky at the minute. It would have been nice if it was today, back in England.”

#1709. Arsenal: 'Much more complete' - how Madueke has grown and become a key man amid injuries

By Axel Clody | 24 Nov 2026 07:45

Noni Madueke's signing by Arsenal divided opinion before the forward had even stepped onto the pitch.

Arriving from Chelsea for £50m, the Englishman joined a squad that already had Bukayo Saka as the owner of the right wing and had to justify an investment in a player who initially seemed destined to be a back-up.

A little over a year later, the debate is taking on another dimension. With Saka injured, Madueke has been given a longer run of opportunities and has taken the chance. As well as goals and assists, he has contributed in different roles on both sides of the pitch. The 2-2 draw with Newcastle, in which he scored the goal that earned Arsenal a point, was another example of this development.

Mikel Arteta has noticed a change that goes beyond productivity. In a press conference, the manager highlighted the variety that the forward has added to the team's play and his contribution without the ball. And Madueke's growth has followed a concrete path.

Madueke has very specific characteristics. Left-footed and explosive, he likes to receive the ball wide on the right, run at the full-back and carry the ball towards the box to shoot or find a team-mate. His short burst of acceleration and ability to change direction make his movements hard to defend when he receives the ball in equal-numbers situations.

That characteristic was already visible at Chelsea. In the 2024-25 season, he was one of the Premier League players who carried the ball into the box the most and created danger mainly through individual runs. The problem was inconsistency in execution: he did not always choose the best moment. Arteta acknowledged the change.

'He is becoming decisive in games, and that is what we need from our forward players. And he is doing it in several ways, which is something I really like. He has added variety and a lot more connection to his game' - Arteta said.

The numbers help to gauge the growth. According to FotMob's analysis for the 2026-27 Premier League, Madueke creates 3.6 chances per 90 minutes, compared with 1.5 for Saka. It is a significant difference, although it is important to consider that Saka has played fewer minutes.

The improvement also shows in his ability to contribute without the ball. According to Arteta, Madueke does not always need to receive the ball at his feet to take part in the move.

'And yes, I also love his intensity without the ball. So, I would say he is becoming a much more complete player, and I think he is enjoying it a lot' - Arteta said.

The evolution, therefore, is not about abandoning the dribble but about knowing when to use it. Madueke remains a player of individual initiative, only now he seems to understand better how his actions can connect with the collective workings of the team.

The comparison with Saka is inevitable, but the two are not identical players. Both are left-footed and prefer to start from the right to cut inside, but they do so in different ways.

Saka is more refined in decision-making. He has excellent ball control, protects possession under pressure and alternates between carries, short passes and crosses very naturally. His ability to draw two markers and find the free team-mate is also one of Arsenal's main attacking tools.

Madueke, for his part, offers more explosiveness in the first movement and tends to look for the individual duel more often. He is a more vertical player, who likes to accelerate and attack the space left by the full-back. When he is confident, he can disorganise a defence without depending on a long build-up.

The creation data helps illustrate this difference. As well as outperforming Saka in chances created per 90 minutes in FotMob's analysis, Madueke also shows a greater volume of dribbles and progressive carries per minute in another statistical comparison this season. Saka, on the other hand, keeps the advantage in shooting and defensive contribution indicators. They are complementary profiles, not necessarily competitors for a single way of playing.

This difference is valuable for Arteta. Against opponents who defend in a low block, Saka can be more useful to control possession, combine with the midfielders and find the pass that dismantles the marking. Madueke can offer a more direct threat, attacking the full-back and creating situations of individual imbalance.

The Englishman has also shown that he can play on the left, a role he performed when Christos Tzolis was unavailable. There, he needs to adapt his movements: instead of cutting inside with his dominant foot, he can look for the byline and cross with his right. It is not necessarily his ideal position, but the versatility widens Arteta's options and prevents the team from depending on a single alternative for each side.

The competition with Saka, therefore, does not need to be understood as an attempt to take the starter's place. Arsenal need more than one player capable of deciding matches, especially in a long season, with the Premier League, the Champions League and domestic cups. The point is that Madueke is starting to offer arguments to be considered more than a simple replacement.

One detail of this transformation happened away from Arsenal. After being left out of an England squad, Madueke decided to use the international break to train individually. Instead of treating the period as a chance to rest, the forward sought out a specific preparation programme.

Arteta highlighted the player's reaction as an example for the rest of the squad. The manager said that Madueke came back from the break as a different athlete, determined not to accept the situation he was in.

Premier League 2025-26 vs. 2026-27, per-90 averages

Premier League games only. Because the seasons have different numbers of minutes, the comparison uses per-90 averages; the total appears below each average. The change compares the averages. Madueke has not yet provided an assist in the Premier League in 2026-27. Data up to 21 November 2026 (matchweek 11).

'He went away, decided to train, came back, and he was a different Noni. You could sense that he meant business, and he was not going to accept that situation. Since then, he has been incredible' - Arteta explained, commenting on the player's change of attitude.

The individual work, however, did not start now. In an interview with Sky Sports, Madueke revealed that he has been working for years with specialist coach Saul Isaksson-Hurst, since his time at PSV. The partnership involves technical improvement and individual development, with special attention to the ability to be more decisive in the final third.

The result has shown up in the numbers: his average of chances created has more than doubled compared with last season, reaching 3.57 per 90 minutes in the Premier League. His dribble success rate has risen from 50% to 55%, while his passing accuracy has gone from 78% to 87%. In open-play crosses, his success rate has jumped from 14% to 33%.

These numbers help explain why Arteta talks about a more complete player. Madueke has not stopped looking for the dribble, but he has started to execute better other actions that previously could limit his influence. The progress has come from different reasons and paths, but the result has arrived and is evident in the current season.

#1708. ‘Incredible’ Arsenal dropped two points in Dortmund draw – Madueke

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Arsenal dropped two points in their 1-1 Champions League draw against Borussia Dortmund, so says Noni Madueke.

The Gunners were dominant in the first half at Emirates Stadium, where Viktor Gyokeres' stunner put them into a 10th-minute lead.

Yet Arsenal could not add to their lead, and Dortmund stepped up in the second half, equalising in the 55th minute through Maximilian Beier.

Jobe Bellingham saw a goal disallowed, but Arsenal came on strong late on, with Gyokeres squandering a golden chance, while the Gunners hit the post twice.

Arsenal's 30 shots are their most on record in a Champions League game (since 2003-04), and the Gunners' most in a game that they failed to win across all competitions since December 2023 v West Ham.

And while Madueke felt some of Arsenal's play was "incredible", he acknowledged Mikel Arteta's team are frustrated.

He told Amazon Prime: "I feel like the performance from us up until the last shot was incredible at times.

"Definitely feels like two points dropped. A bit of frustration; need to get all three points, I think."

Honours even in N5. https://t.co/quJELEQP8x

Gyokeres echoed Madueke's sentiment, though he is confident Arsenal will get better results if they keep on creating so many chances.

"We could have scored in the second half. We could have won the game in many different ways," he told Amazon Prime.

"We played well and created a lot of chances, we deserved to win the game but sometimes it is like that.

"The most important thing is that we create those chances and get shots on goal. For sure we will score goals."

Arsenal have failed to win a home game in the group stage of major European competition for the first time since November 2019 (2-1 defeat v Eintracht Frankfurt), ending a run of 18 successive victories – the longest such winning run by any side in major European competition history.

Arteta said: "The performance was superb and there is no question about that from the start to the end. We played against a really good side and the domination and threat was really impressive. The general feeling inside the dressing room is that we should reward ourselves with more.

"I love the courage, the fluidity and the understanding with the players with and without the ball."

The Gunners are, though, only the third English side in Champions League history to go 20 successive matches unbeaten (W14 D6), after Manchester City between 2022 and 2024 (26) and Manchester United between 2007 and 2009 (25).

Now, their focus will turn to a huge Premier League clash with Man City on Sunday.

"I think these are the best games. I'm really looking forward to it," Madueke added.

"Two draws on the bounce now and I just desperately want to win on the weekend and I know my team-mates feel the same.

"We are going to do everything we have to win the three points. We're champions, we're at home. We have a duty to perform well at the Emirates. There are things we need to improve but all in all we are going in the right direction."

#1707. Arsenal: Mikel Arteta issues fresh David Raya injury update ahead of Man City showdown

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Mikel Arteta provided a coy update on David Raya’s availability for Arsenal’s showdown with Manchester City this weekend.

The goalkeeper missed the Gunners’ draw with Borussia Dortmund on Tuesday night with a shoulder injury that he picked up against Newcastle.

The Spaniard left the pitch at St James’ Park in significant pain and Arsenal feared a lengthy absence, but scans proved to be positive.

The No1 has avoided a serious injury and he will not require surgery, though there is uncertainty over exactly when he will return.

There are suggestions that the goalkeeper will only be out for a matter of days and could be in contention to face City on Sunday.

“No, we have nothing to add today unfortunately,” Arteta said after his side’s 1-1 draw with Dortmund.

“We need to know first how bad it is and whether he has a chance or not [to face Man City].”

In Raya’s absence, Kepa Arrizabalaga started against Dortmund, as Arsenal had to settle for just a point despite a dominant performance.

The Spaniard was fairly comfortable throughout, though he did have some shaky moments from corners and when rolling the ball out to Myles Lewis-Skelly to play him into trouble.

However, it was an improvement on Kepa’s display in the Carabao Cup final last season and solid enough to be confident he will keep his place over Illan Meslier while Raya remains out.

Kepa has had limited football since joining the club, so trusted has Raya become for Arsenal, but Arteta insisted he will have full faith in the goalkeeper if he is required to start in goal against City.

“Him and Illan, they’re both in the same situation,” Arteta said.

“I think Kepa had a really good performance today. We fully trust our keepers and if he needs to play against City, he will play.”

#1706. James Tarkowski: Games Everton defender will miss as red card leaves David Moyes with “big problem”

By Oliver Thomas | 24 Nov 2026 08:40, Last updated: 24 Nov 2026 08:42

James Tarkowski received his first-ever red card in the Premier League as Everton fell to a heavy 4-0 defeat at Brentford on Monday night.

The 34-year-old defender had previously been given 74 yellow cards across 350 Premier League appearances but had never been sent off – a top-flight record for the most yellows without ever seeing red.

However, Tarkowski was dismissed in the first half with the Toffees trailing by two goals at the Gtech Community Stadium for a studs-up challenge on the shin of Yehor Yarmolyuk.

Tarkowski had initially thundered into a sliding challenge and won the ball, but his right boot followed through with his studs scraping down the Brentford midfielder’s leg.

On-field referee Craig Pawson gave a yellow card for the challenge, but was then advised by VAR to review the incident at the pitchside monitor, where he ultimately came to the decision to upgrade the yellow to a red.

Tarkowski was deemed to have “committed a challenge that endangers his opponent's safety” with a red card issued for serious foul play.

James Tarkowski is sent off! ? https://t.co/s5ta4f74np

Tarkowski will therefore serve a three-match suspension and will crucially miss Sunday’s Merseyside derby against rivals Liverpool at the Hill Dickinson Stadium.

The Toffees captain is also banned for a trip to Aston Villa on December 2 and a home clash with Fulham four days later, but he is available to return for an away fixture against Brighton & Hove Albion on December 13.

After taking charge of his record-breaking 593rd game as Everton manager, David Moyes was asked whether the club will look to appeal the red card, and he told Sky Sports: "Don't know yet.

"I thought Tarki got the ball in plenty of time, certainly got there before the player who came in late, but I think Tarki's foot was high, and in that case then there is a chance it can be given."

Speaking to BBC Match of the Day, Moyes added: "My thoughts at the time, I didn't think it was, but when I've looked at it again I think his foot high. Is there enough force for it to be a red card? Not sure about that."

Sky Sports pundit and former Liverpool defender Jamie Carragher believes that Tarkowski was right to be sent off and feels that Moyes has a “big problem” to deal with ahead of the Merseyside derby.

"It is a red card. It might not have been a red card in 1996, but it is in 2026,” Carragher said on Monday Night Football.

"He knows what he's doing, and he doesn't need to do that. At the last moment, he is trying to pull back on the intensity of the challenge. Don't give [the referee] the option. He doesn't need to do that. I've made tackles like that."

He added: "David Moyes should be looking at him and thinking [it's 2-0], you've left your mates out there with 10, and it's the Merseyside derby next.

"For me, it's the biggest game of the season. Everton, biggest game of the season. I hope for the Liverpool players and staff, the biggest game of the season.

"He's brilliant in the box, and that will be a big problem for Everton. He's so good set-piece-wise."

Either Jake O'Brien or Michael Keane is expected to play at centre-back alongside Jarrad Branthwaite in the absence of Tarkowski in the next three Premier League games.

A four-goal defeat for Everton has seen them slip to ninth in the Premier League table, with Brentford leapfrogging them into seventh position, albeit sitting just one point above them.

#1705. Arsenal told penalty verdict as Viktor Gyokeres ‘gets away’ with Borussia Dortmund controversy

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Arsenal were fortunate not to concede a penalty against Borussia Dortmund during their Champions League draw.

The Premier League champions and Bundesliga leaders held each other to a 1-1 stalemate at the Emirates Stadium, as Viktor Gyokeres’ rifled opener was cancelled out in the second half by Maximilian Beier.

It was the Gunners’ second draw on the spin after a 2-2 encounter at St James’ Park, where Noni Madueke rescued a point against Newcastle after Malick Thiaw and Harvey Barnes had put the Magpies ahead following Eberechi Eze’s opening goal.

But it was the goalscorer Gyokeres who almost turned from hero to villain, as he allegedly handled a Dortmund corner in the second period.

It led Amazon Prime Video pundits Alan Shearer and Mark Clattenberg to question referee Maurizio Mariani’s decision not to award a spot kick to the visitors.

“I think Arsenal were fortunate to have gotten away with that one,” Shearer said on co-commentary.

"I know it might have been Fabio Silva in front of him trying to flick it on, but he didn't, and his arm is actually out."

Clattenberg, said alongside the record Premier League goalscorer in the north London gantry, concurred.

"We all know UEFA have a stricter handball rule than we see in the Premier League, but what doesn't save Gyokeres in this situation is, the ball comes in from a distance and he makes a little movement of his arm towards the ball so that makes it look more like a penalty kick for me,” the former official said.

Former Arsenal forward Theo Walcott spoke of his relief at the penalty not being given.

"As soon as it hit his hand, straight away my heart is in my mouth, I think it's a penalty," he said.

"I think he's got away with that. I'm pleased it wasn't given because it's not a penalty, but in Europe it probably should be."

Gyokeres asserted his innocence in his post-match interview.

"I think the arm was towards my body," the Swede said.

"I don't think it was outside, so I don't think it was anything."

#1704. Cardinale praises ‘fantastic’ Milan and admits he ‘expects to compete’ for the Scudetto

Gerry Cardinale gave his thoughts after watching his AC Milan side run riot against Frosinone at San Siro this evening.

It has been yet another few days where the Milan owner has made his presence felt. After landing in Italy, he was at Milanello and Casa Milan on Saturday for a series of important meetings with the management and the squad, and then he watched first hand as the Rossoneri won tonight.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

An own-goal from Gabriele Calvani got the scoring going, before Goncalo Ramos, Ardon Jashari, Alphadjo Cisse and Christian Pulisic all scored in the 5-1 rout of Frosinone. It could have been more in truth, but it was another display of the level this team can play at.

Cardinale was interviewed by Michael Cuomo of TeleLombardia after the final whistle having made his way down from the stands, and his comments were relayed by MilanNews.

“Well, I’m never satisfied, but the results speak for themselves. The boys were fantastic tonight. I hope you’re happy. I hope the fans are happy. I think the team is coming together really well.

“It’s a game, let’s keep it under control, but I’m really proud of the boys. This is a team. It’s a team that wants to win until the end.”

“Look, it’s November. We still have a long way to go. But we want to see improvements in every match. This weekend was very interesting if you look at the kind of results we’ve had. You can see that something is changing in Serie A.

“I was very happy to see us not just win, but win by that margin. And so, we have to build on that, but as Amorim says, every match is something to build on, and we have a long way to go. I personally still expect us to compete for the Scudetto, but it’s a long way off. One match at a time.

“Now the focus is on the Europa League. Yes, and as Ruben said, we have to do both. European competitions are important. Everything is a test. If you want to win a Scudetto, you have to do it all the way, and that’s what we’ll do.”

“Again: January is just another stage. As you know, the January transfer window is complicated. You have to be disciplined. You can’t just jump into something randomly. The only thing that will happen under my ownership is that every time we play in the transfer market, we’ll play to win.

“That’s the theme. That’s the theme I said at the beginning of this year. So, if we make a move in any transfer window, January or June, it will be a move that will count.”

#1703. Man United CEO Omar Berrada insists the team have IMPROVED since the transfer window in his first interview in five months - but does accept criticism of leadership has been fair

Published: 10:25 EST, 20 November 2026 | Updated: 11:32 EST, 20 November 2026

Manchester United CEO Omar Berrada insists the team got 'fundamentally better' after this summer's transfer window, as he warned ‘spending just for the sake of it’ is not the route to putting United back on top.

In his first sit-down interview in five months, Berrada tackled topics ranging from the relationship between the Glazers and Ineos, the imminent departure of youngster JJ Gabriel, the decision not to sign a left back in the summer, as well as the decision to push ahead for a new stadium despite supporter backlash on matchdays.

The United chief has been at the centre of furious protests and anti-ownership chanting at matches this season, alongside Director of Football Jason Wilcox, and he accepted that criticism of United's leadership has, mostly, been fair.

In an interview that aired shortly after new head coach Mauricio Pochettino spoke to the media for the first time, Berrada was pressed on how much accountability falls at his door with United heading to Anfield this weekend 18th in the Premier League table.

'I think if you think about the fact we've had three permanent managers in less than three seasons, clearly we haven't achieved the stability that we wanted, that's for sure,' Berrada told Sky Sports.

'When it doesn't work out with the coach or the manager, we are all responsible. Myself, the football leadership, everyone who is involved around the coach and the staff and the players. We have to continue improving and getting better.

Manchester United's CEO Omar Berrada finally fronted up in an interview with Sky Sports

Michael Carrick's sacking was yet another managerial change at United, with the hierarchy under massive scrutiny and Mauricio Pochettino now in the hotseat

'There are different circumstances why it didn't work out with Erik [ten Hag], and Ruben [Amorim], and now Michael [Carrick], and we are always learning and, as I said, trying to improve and understand what has failed.

'The challenge is we're trying to find the right manager for the squad that we have with a specific set of skills in that moment to make them perform at their best level.

'It's true, we have to accept the criticism that we haven't been able to achieve that stability with one coach and our aim is to do that as soon as possible. Of course, we hope now that Mauricio coming in will give us that stability that I think we all need.'

Berrada's links to Manchester City, where he worked prior to joining United, were brought up, not least given he worked at the club during the period that City have had charges brought against them.

But at his new home there are issues aplenty, not least having got another managerial appointment wrong, sacking Carrick less than six months after handing him a two-year deal, and so it was put to Berrada: is the club actually progressing?

'It's not good enough, not acceptable and that's why we've made the change that we made so that we can move forward,' he concluded.

(L-R) Sir Jim Ratcliffe, Berrada and Jason Wilcox have drawn plenty of ire from Man United fans

'But we are laying the foundations for sustained growth, to put us in a position where we can be competitive consistently. It's not always been that.

'Last year we finished third, we were happy with the squad, we were happy with the way we were going. And now, a few months later, we are not where we need to be. But the foundations are there and I am convinced that we are heading in the right direction. Very positive.'

#1701. Barcelona transfer news: Catalan giants could receive £10m windfall from PSG transfer

By Axel Clody | 24 Nov 2026 08:45

Paris Saint-Germain could indirectly do Barcelona a favour in the January transfer window. In search of a potential attacking reinforcement after the long-term injuries to Khvicha Kvaratskhelia and Desire Doue, the capital club have drawn up an initial shortlist.

According to AS, Antonio Nusa is among the capital club's preferred targets, alongside Abde Ezzalzouli, Gianluca Prestianni, Ibrahim Maza, Luis Diaz and Estevao. These players will be difficult to sign in the January transfer window. Paris have already experienced that, having been rebuffed over Estevao, while Prestianni wants to finish the season at Benfica.

In that sense, Abde Ezzalzouli could be an interesting option. 3Cat confirms that the Morocco international is among the targets being studied by PSG to strengthen their attack in January. Aged 24, Abde is enjoying a good start to the season, with four goals and one assist in 13 games for the Andalusian club.

His profile has reportedly caught the attention of the Parisian hierarchy, especially as the player now shares the same agent as Achraf Hakimi.

This could ease discussions. The rumour is also being followed closely in Barcelona, as a potential transfer of the Real Betis winger would allow Barcelona to recoup a significant sum.

The Catalan outlet recalls that in September 2023, Barcelona sold Abde to Real Betis for £6.4m (€7.5m). In that deal, they kept a share of the Moroccan's economic rights. Initially set at 50%, it was later reduced to 20% in February 2025 as part of the agreement concerning Vitor Roque.

A £51m (€60m) transfer, the amount of Abde's release clause, would therefore bring Barcelona £10m. PSG would have the opportunity to sign a promising 24-year-old winger for a reasonable amount, while doing their Spanish rivals a serious financial favour by triggering the clause.

This sum could give the Barcelona hierarchy more room for manoeuvre to strengthen Hansi Flick's squad this winter. The German boss is notably looking to sign a centre-back.

It should be noted that, at this stage, no agreement or advanced negotiation has been announced for Abde's arrival at PSG. It remains to be seen whether Paris will actually take action.

#1700. Hellberg: Boro’s win at Swansea best way to celebrate one year in charge

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Kim Hellberg said there was no better way to celebrate his one-year anniversary in charge of Middlesbrough by earning another victory in the Championship on Tuesday.

A year on from being appointed as the club's second overseas-born head coach, Hellberg led his side back to the top of the table with a 2-1 win at home to Swansea City.

Myles Peart-Harris opened the scoring at the Riverside Stadium in the ninth minute before Joseph Opoku levelled things up for the visitors 13 minutes later.

However, the Championship's top scorer, Will Lankshear, swept home his 14th league goal of the season nine minutes into the second half to seal the win for Middlesbrough.

Middlesbrough have now won seven of their last nine league games against Swansea (D1 L1), as they moved one point clear at the top of the second tier.

Hellberg's side missed out on promotion to the Championship in 2025-26 after losing to Hull City in the play-off final, but the Middlesbrough boss was not getting too far ahead of himself, instead focusing on this Friday's clash with Southampton, their opponents amid the "Spygate" controversy last season.

"That makes it one year, 46 league games. It was a nice way to celebrate that," Hellberg said.

"I think over 90 minutes we were quite good against a different challenge from the last game. It was more of an attacking game.

"I think we should have scored more goals, but we take 2-1 today and move on to Friday [against Southampton].

"Happy with the performance, happy with how much we created and happy with how few chances we gave away, even if they could have scored another one.

"I always felt we would create enough chances to win."

A familiar celebration to complete a year in charge https://t.co/YDbyUArilk

— Middlesbrough FC (@Boro) November 24, 2026

Wolves remain firmly in the hunt for automatic promotion back to the Premier League, with Cesar Peixoto's side thumping struggling Derby County 3-0 at Molineux.

Mateus Mane netted either side of Adam Armstrong's brace to pile the pressure on Derby boss John Eustace, who has seen his side lose four of their last five league matches.

Scott Parker is still waiting for his first win in charge of West Ham, with Odin Bailey's 31st-minute goal enough to earn Portsmouth a deserved 1-0 victory.

Preston North End hauled themselves off the foot of the table by thumping Cardiff City 4-0, while Charlton Athletic won by the same scoreline at home to Lincoln City.

The Argentine is said to be keen to add a striker to his squad, with Benjamin Sesko struggling for fitness and Joshua Zirkzee for form.

Arsenal have begun talks with RB Leipzig over signing winger Antonio Nusa in a deal which could be worth £67million.

The 21-year-old has impressed this season, registering six goals and eight assists in 15 appearances, prompting Arsenal to send scouts to watch him in action against Manchester City.

According to Fabrizio Romano, Leipzig would be reluctant to sell Nusa midway through the season following the departure of Yan Diomande last summer.

Any January deal would likely require an exceptional offer, although interest in the winger is growing ahead of 2027.

Arsenal are viewed as a strong potential destination given their need for a left-sided attacker, but Paris Saint-Germain are also monitoring his progress.

Chelsea may have cooled their interest in Alex Scott and Lamine Camara.

The Blues were expected to at least make a swoop for Bournemouth stars Scott, and have been linked with reigniting their pursuit of Monaco man Camara.

But The Athletic’s David Ornstein is not so sure.

“When you look back to the end of the summer window, Chelsea didn’t get let’s say a Kone, a Camara and Alex Scott but I’m not aware of them going for those players this January, maybe that’s something for the summer.

“When you look at the rise of Romeo Lavia now he appears to be staying fit, he’s one of the best midfielders in his position available.”

Paris Saint-Germain could step up their pursuit of Bournemouth forward Eli Junior Kroupi after Desire Doue suffered a serious knee injury, Teamtalk claims.

The injury comes just a month after Khvicha Kvaratskhelia suffered an ACL injury that is expected to keep him out for at least 6 months.

Kroupi is seen as the next starlet in France and PSG could act in January given their injuries.

Paris Saint-Germain are preparing to offer midfielder Vitinha a new contract until 2032, according to Nico Schira.

The Portuguese’s agent, Jorge Mendes, is thought to be braced for an approach from the European champions.

Sky Germany reports that Bayern Munich are weighing up a move for Schalke 04 goalkeeper Loris Karius.

However, the 33-year-old says he hasn’t spoken to anyone about a potential transfer.

Diario Sport claims that Barcelona now face competition from Chelsea, Manchester United and Manchester City for FC Twente defender Ruud Nijstad.

Barca have been leading the race for the 18-year-old, but Twente’s asking price of over €20million could complicate a January move.

#1697. Kevin De Bruyne responds to Man City "disgrace" claims after Premier League guilty verdict

By Oliver Thomas | 24 Nov 2026 09:01, Last updated: 24 Nov 2026 10:51

Kevin De Bruyne has made his feelings for Manchester City crystal clear as he has spoken out for the first time since the club were found guilty of breaching Premier League financial regulations.

At the end of September, an independent commission found Man City guilty of all charges related to serious breaches of the Premier League’s financial rules and the majority of charges in relation to its failure to co-operate with the investigation.

The Citizens are accused of using "sham" contracts with a number of commercial partners to disguise secret funding of more than £830m and artificially inflate revenues between the 2009-10 and 2017-18 seasons.

Man City continue to plead their innocence and lodged an appeal last month, stating that “a comprehensive body of irrefutable evidence exists in support of all of its positions, relating to this case.”

A plethora of possible sanctions have been mooted should Man City’s guilty verdict be upheld, including heavy fines, transfer bans, stripping titles, points deductions leading to relegation and expulsion from the Premier League.

De Bruyne spent 10 glorious years at the Etihad Stadium before leaving in the summer of 2025 and will go down as one of Man City’s greatest-ever players after playing a crucial role in the club winning 19 trophies during his time at the club.

The Belgian playmaker won six Premier League titles, five EFL Cups and three FA Cups, while he also won the Champions League during a historic treble-winning season in 2022-23.

The two-time Premier League Player of the Season scored 108 goals and provided 177 assists in 422 appearances for Man City across all competitions, with 119 of those assists recorded in the Premier League to rank him second on the all-time list behind Ryan Giggs (162).

De Bruyne has made a welcome retuned to Manchester as his current club Napoli prepare to face City in the Champions League on Tuesday night.

While De Bruyne has acknowledged that some people may have different opinions over Man City’s guilty verdict, the legendary midfielder himself has insisted that his feelings towards the club will “never change”.

"My feeling's never been different,” he told reporters at a press conference. “Honestly, the way that I feel is just the way that I've been treated by this club, what I've done with this club for me personally, and how we've worked together as a group. Of course, it's a lot of things that's been going on but I cannot change anything about that.

"I'm proud of what I've done as a football player, and honestly... This is my club! I love the owners, I've talked about a lot of stuff outside of football, I've even spoken to Khaldoon [Al Mubarak] how to buy a club and everything, so there's a lot of things that goes around after this.

"I've nothing but affection for this club and that will never change! Even now, the people who treated me for 10 years exceptionally, my family and everything, that's for me the most important and for me, that is it to be honest."

Intense criticism has been aimed at Man City since the guilty verdict, but De Bruyne cannot "change anything" about people calling his former club a "disgrace" and still believes that everything he personally achieved with the club was won fairly.

“It [the verdict] still doesn’t change, my football has not changed,” De Bruyne said. “In life there are rules, but everybody plays on the limit.

“I played in between the white lines, I competed with other players and I had many experiences with my teams, with the players. That’s the thing I value most.

“In my career, the most important thing is the relationships between everybody that I had and how you manage these things.

“I’ve given my all and that’s not going to change in my mind. I don’t think a lot of ­people will change in their mind how they view me as a player or how we played. Other people may be disgraced a bit, but I can’t change anything about that.”

Tuesday’s contest will mark De Bruyne’s second appearance back at the Etihad since departing Man City, and the 35-year-old will be hoping for a much smoother evening this time around.

On his previous visit last year, a first-half red card forced ex-Napoli boss Antonio Conte to reshuffle his side, with De Bruyne the unfortunate player to be sacrificed early in a 2-0 defeat.

#1696. McInnes wants a quiet January... but it might just be the right time for Rangers to cash in on Raskin

Published: 11:37 EST, 20 November 2026 | Updated: 11:44 EST, 20 November 2026

Derek McInnes can be understood in wanting a quiet January window. He’s still bonding a squad of players together. Drama and diversions are the last thing he needs when there looks to be an opportunity to win a title on the horizon.

In the case of Olwethu Makhanya, for example, this is definitely not the time to sell.

The 22-year-old South African has been impressive at centre-back, but it will take a campaign catching the attention in high-level European football for him to raise his value to Calvin Bassey levels and beyond.

Same goes for the likes of Ryan Naderi. Getting into the Czechia squad and increasing his range of experience makes him a more interesting prospect, but UEFA competition is a platform that ought to increase his premium.

McInnes, as he did this week, has to say he wants to keep his more prominent talents anyway. It would be strange to appear accepting of the board cashing in on bigger players.

When it comes to Nico Raskin, however, things are different. A buyer for him should have been found in the summer after his World Cup involvement with Belgium.

Rangers midfielder Nico Raskin is an asset who could be sold in the January transfer window

From the chit-chat around the game, it does not seem unreasonable to think Rangers maybe overvalued him in the initial part of that window and missed the boat in terms of securing a sale.

If he stays for the rest of this season and enters the final year of his contract, though, the money you can ask for naturally reduces. The club might seek to tie him up on a new deal, of course, but his remarks about being ‘mentally ready to leave’ at the start of the season point to the most likely direction of travel.

Is he irreplaceable? Not at all. And this is where forward planning should come into the mix.

If there’s someone out there willing to edge anywhere close to the £15m mark for the 25-year-old, they should be getting sounded out now – with a contingency plan being discussed and worked on in tandem.

Yes, Rangers need to get back to winning silverware, but the need to start raising funds through selling players – and replacing them - at appropriate times is pressing too.

As often said here, they can’t keep spending money the way they have been without considerably more coming back in return.

Raskin’s a good player, but his three-and-a-half years at Ibrox have hardly been shaped by his propensity for winning medals, have they? If a realistic fee is there in January, there’s a case to make for it being taken.

#1695. Arsenal can equal two all-time Champions League records in Borussia Dortmund battle

By Ben Knapton | 24 Nov 2026 09:09

Arsenal will be bidding to equal two all-time Champions League records when they welcome Borussia Dortmund to the Emirates Stadium for Tuesday's league-phase encounter.

Mikel Arteta's men reunite with the German giants 12 years on from their last head-to-head in November 2014, when the Spaniard captained Arsenal to a 2-0 victory in North London.

The Gunners could end the evening top of the Champions League league phase table too, if they overcome Dortmund and Real Madrid - who are two points clear - either lose to PSV Eindhoven or draw and fall behind on goal difference; Paris Saint-Germain are not in action until Wednesday.

Arsenal have accrued 10 points from their opening four continental games this season, overcoming Lille, Slavia Prague and Napoli and only dropping points in an encapsulating 2-2 draw away to Bayern Munich.

After also navigating the entire 2025-26 league phase unbeaten, Arsenal could firstly equal their own club record of 17 straight Champions League group stage/league phase games without suffering defeat.

Arteta's men have won 15 and drawn one of their 16 league-phase games since a 1-0 loss to Inter Milan in November 2024, and they have only ever gone 17 unbeaten at this stage between 2003 and 2006.

That record streak began with a 1-0 victory over Dynamo Kyiv in November 2003, and ended when Arsene Wenger's men suffered a 1-0 defeat to CSKA Moscow in 2006.

Additionally, Arsenal have won each of their last 12 Champions League group stage/league phase games at the Emirates and could equal the English football record for the longest victorious run on home soil.

The only Premier League team to win more successive UCL league phase/group stage games at home is Liverpool, who triumphed in 13 on the spin between 2020 and 2025.

Ever since their return to the Champions League in the 2023-24 season, Arsenal have been almost perfect at home in the group stage/league phase, and their 12-game winning run is a sight to behold.

Arteta's side kicked off their triumphant streak with a 4-0 rout of PSV Eindhoven in September 2023, before Sevilla and Lens were bested in the same year.

The 2024-25 group stage saw Paris Saint-Germain, Shakhtar Donetsk, Monaco and Dinamo Zagreb conquered in North London, while Olympiacos, Bayern Munich, Atletico Madrid and Kairat Almaty fell to Arsenal's Emirates might in 2025-26.

The Gunners' only home encounter in Europe so far this season ended in a 3-0 success over Lille, and they have scored a remarkable 36 goals while conceding just three during their 12-match sequence.

Thanks to Arsenal's prolonged absence from the Champions League between 2017 and 2023, it has been almost exactly 10 years since they last failed to win a group stage/league phase game at the Emirates; a 2-2 draw with Paris Saint-Germain on November 23, 2016.

#1694. Contract talks ‘irrelevant’ amid Man Utd’s poor form, says Fernandes

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Bruno Fernandes insisted his focus remained on turning Manchester United's fortunes around rather than putting pen to paper on a new contract at Old Trafford.

Fernandes, who returns to Sporting CP with United in the Champions League on Wednesday, has been linked with a move away from the Red Devils over the last few years.

The 32-year-old was the subject of interest from the Saudi Pro League, while it has been reported he has turned down two offers to extend his stay with United.

Fernandes has a deal at Old Trafford until the end of the season, although the club hold an option to extend it through to June 2028, but the United captain's priorities lie on the pitch.

United were thumped 4-0 by rivals Liverpool in Mauricio Pochettino's first game in charge, a result that leaves them 19th in the Premier League after 11 matches of the campaign.

Indeed, United's eight points this season are their fewest after 11 games of a league campaign since 1972-73 (seven). That is also the previous season in which the Red Devils only managed one win in their first 11 league matches.

"For us to start winning games, and then we can start speaking about a contract," Fernandes told reporters when asked about his future. "That's not important now, it's irrelevant.

"Obviously, I know it's my future, and I probably shouldn't look at it that way because I haven't got much left in my contract, but I'm not really worried about that.

"I'm more worried about getting results, trying to bring the club back into a position that we can be proud of, and we're not there at the moment.

"We're going to have time to speak about that. As I said, we had conversations.

"The conversations stopped at the moment that we thought that was not as important at the moment because results and performances were not at the level we should be."

"There's still time for me to learn and become better." @B_Fernandes8 remains hungrier than ever to improve as a player and help the team https://t.co/PRwzDbI2G2

— Manchester United (@ManUtd) November 24, 2026

Fernandes joined United from Sporting in January 2020 and has become a crucial part of the Red Devils' midfield, but only has an FA Cup and EFL Cup to show for his efforts.

In fact, since moving to England, Fernandes has only played in one Champions League knockout tie, coming against Atletico Madrid back in 2022.

"As a player, you want to play the biggest tournaments, the biggest games," Fernandes added. "Sometimes it's not possible.

"When I started my career, I never had the opportunity in the first few years to play in the Champions League, so for me that was a dream far away, and I'm very proud of what I have achieved, even if I have only played one time [in the knockouts].

"I still have got time, I still have got many years left in my career, I hope so, and I'm going to have many opportunities to do that, and why not this season?"

With his penalty against Roma last time out, Fernandes netted his 24th goal in major European competition for United, moving ahead of Cristiano Ronaldo into seventh spot on the club's all-time scoring list, and he will be hoping to have another impact at the Estadio Jose Alvalade.

However, United are winless in their last six Champions League away games (D2 L4), losing both this season. They last had a longer winless run away from home in the competition between February 2004 and December 2005 (eight matches – D3 L5).
