#1645. THE BREAKDOWN: The real reasons why Enzo Maresca's Man City can't stop losing - from anonymous Enzo Fernandez abandoning Elliot Anderson, to the fatal flaws in Italian's set-up that are being brutally exposed

Published: 07:00 EST, 20 November 2026 | Updated: 14:40 EST, 20 November 2026

Diet Pep is losing his fizz. Enzo Maresca may look like Pep Guardiola, may have learned his craft under his Manchester City predecessor, but his quest to follow in his mentor’s footsteps has all gone a bit flat.

Seven successive Premier League wins to start his City reign, a record for a new manager in the competition, breaking one jointly-held by Guardiola, gave the impression that this might be a smooth passing of the torch after all.

Three months in, and three defeats on the spin that left them six points behind Arsenal have made it clear that something is not clicking for Maresca.

Is the uncertainty around the potential punishment following that guilty verdict taking its toll? Is Maresca just suffering from his usual late autumn dips? He suffered similar tricky periods around late October and early November at Leicester and his first season at Chelsea too.

Or is there something at the heart of his side, of his system, that’s finally being exposed?

Enzo Maresca's Man City have slumped to three straight Premier League defeats after a promising start to the season

Guardiola’s City was all about control. Keep the ball, dominate the pitch, play the game at your pace, on your terms.

Maresca’s City, regardless of how well they started the season, has been about anything but. It has been about triumph amid chaos, about moments of magic more than the overarching method.

Without that control, City’s defensive issues have been laid bare. The 13 goals they have let in after 10 games is their most at this stage since 2008. They haven’t kept a clean sheet in their last eight matches in all competitions. That's a drought longer than at any point under Guardiola.

Their biggest problem over City's three successive Premier League defeats is just how susceptible they have been to counter attacks.

Only Newcastle have faced more shots this season following ‘fast breaks’ – data giants Opta's term for counter attacks – than City’s 17, and 11 of those have come in the last three games: six against Nottingham Forest, two of which led to goals, three against Brighton and another two against Aston Villa.

Maresca’s side are being more profligate in possession, too. Over the first seven games of the season, they lost the ball 120 times a game on average – one of the best figures in the division. Since then, it’s closer to 140.

City have been wasteful in possession and regularly overrun on the counter, with Elliot Anderson (centre) too often left isolated in midfield

Many of these problems have their roots in Maresca's serious problems in midfield. Rodri, the best holding midfielder of his generation, was always going to be hard to replace but Maresca appears to be expecting Elliot Anderson to do it all on his own.

Anderson is at his best when he’s free to get up and down the pitch, box to box, using his physicality not just in winning the ball back but progressing it. No midfielder played more passes into the final third last season than Anderson at Forest. At one stage of the campaign, he had played more progressive passes than any other player across Europe’s top five leagues.

And yet Maresca is forcing Anderson to play as the sitter while his golden boy Enzo Fernandez, whom he pushed City to sign in the summer for £125million, is roaming free and high up the pitch.

Maresca likes his teams to build up in a 3-1-6 shape, which sees Fernandez push up as an extra attacking midfielder, and leaves Anderson manning the fort alone.

When City lose the ball, though, it leaves them wide open.

This is the opening goal City conceded against Forest. Josko Gvardiol wants to play the ball inside but has only red shirts and empty green space ahead of him. Anderson is the only man free, but even he is too high and has a Forest player ready to cut off the pass. Eventually, Gvardiol gets robbed and Forest score.

A lack of options for Josko Gvardiol (left) led to Forest's opener against City. Enzo Fernandez (circled) was caught high up the pitch, way ahead of the deeper Anderson (also circled)

Here’s another moment in the defeat by Brighton.

The Seagulls break forward on the flank and Anderson races over to close the ball down. Fernandez is, you guessed it, high up the pitch.

City have no midfield cover to stop the ball inside, Abdukodir Khusanov gets drawn in and leaves loads of space in behind for Yasin Ayari to exploit and cross to Maxim De Cuyper for a great chance.

The lack of protection offered by Anderson and especially the more advanced Fernandez was again on show against Brighton, who were able to exploit the acres of space left in midfield

Fernandez is doing what Maresca wants, but it’s not working. Maresca needs more from him, especially when Anderson’s instincts are to press and harass and bully, which can leave gaps when he does not yet read the game as comprehensively as Rodri.

Anderson sits in the top five for ball recoveries among midfielders to have played 500 minutes this season. Fernandez is in the bottom five. That figure becomes even more alarming when you consider Anderson has created more chances from open play than Fernandez, too.

Ayyoub Bouaddi showed at the World Cup that he had the most similar profile to Rodri. It might be time for Maresca to put some faith in him.

Maresca has always wanted his goalkeeper to be an 11th outfielder. In his one season at Leicester, Mads Hermansen played more passes than any goalkeeper in Championship history. During his time at Chelsea, there was a shaky moment in a draw with Arsenal when loud groans greeted a misplaced pass from Robert Sanchez.

‘I am the guy who asks Robert to do that,’ said Maresca after that game. ‘The moment he stops doing that, he is not going to play.’

Donnarumma, though, for all his (usually) excellent shot-stopping, is anything but a ball-playing goalkeeper. The ball rolled under his foot from a simple back pass against Coventry and so nearly crept over the line. He gifted France an early lead while on international duty with Italy when he passed the ball straight to Michael Olise.

Only two keepers made more errors leading to shots than Donnarumma across the course of last season, with many of those being with his feet, like when he gifted Kai Havertz an equaliser in City's victory over Arsenal in April.

Gianluigi Donnarumma has never been good with his feet - now his excellent shot-stopping has taken a dip too

The Italian should have easily dealt with Nicolas Jackson's second goal in City's 2-1 loss at Aston Villa

The decision to let James Trafford leave in the summer, especially with Guardiola’s impending departure and a manager like Maresca coming in, is looking ever more misguided.

Trafford is not immune to mistakes either, of course. He erred badly when trying to play out from the back for City against Spurs last season and made an almost identical howler for Leeds at Bournemouth in October. But he is still far more confident at playing out from the back than Donnarumma.

The double blow for Maresca is that the trade-off with Donnarumma – where he makes up for his weakness with the ball at his feet by making saves that other keepers can’t make – is no longer paying off either.

Nicolas Jackson’s shot squirmed straight through him to hand Villa victory and condemn City to their first defeat of the season.

When you are coughing up chances as frequently as City are, Maresca needs his keeper to be on top form.

Do you know who is keeping the ball out of his net? James Trafford. He boasts the highest save percentage of any goalkeeper in the top flight, keeping out 81 per cent of the shots on target coming his way. Donnarumma is 15th, on less than 66 per cent.

According to Opta’s expected data, Trafford has also prevented more than four goals that he should have conceded from the quality of the shots he’s faced. Again, he’s the best in the Premier League. Donnarumma is middle of the pack.

‘At the moment, I’m not thinking about the goalkeeping situation,’ said Maresca recently. Without Trafford there and just 34-year-old Geronimo Rulli as back-up, he doesn’t really have a choice but to persist with Donnarumma and hope he improves.

When the goals stop flowing for Erling Haaland, City can't mask all their other problems.

So used are we now to seeing the Norwegian on the scoresheet, having notched nine in City’s opening eight matches, that when he goes just two games without a goal it feels as if he’s on a barren spell.

The issue, though, is less down to Haaland and more that City’s build-up in recent weeks is struggling to get him into the game.

City are finding it more difficult to get Haaland on the ball. His touches per game are falling steadily but, crucially, so are the quality of the chances his team-mates are creating for him.

Haaland had more than one Opta-defined 'big chance' in five of City’s opening seven games. He’s had just one come his way in each of their three defeats.

His expected goals (xG) tally is dropping too. Across City’s winning streak, Haaland’s average xG per match was 0.81. Only once, against Liverpool, did it drop below 0.5.

Over the three defeats, it’s just 0.45 and has not once gone above 0.5.

Antoine Semenyo missing the last three games through injury has not helped, especially when teams now try to pack the middle of the pitch and force City wide.

Haaland will come good, he always does, but City need to start serving him again if Maresca wants to get through this tricky spell and stop the vultures from circling.

By Oliver Thomas | 24 Nov 2026 12:22

Liverpool are reportedly among a number of clubs interested in signing Borussia Monchengladbach wonderkid Wael Mohya.

Earlier this month, the 17-year-old attacker earned his first-ever senior international call-up to Jurgen Klopp’s Germany squad after making a notable impression as a first-team regular at club level.

Mohya broke into Monchengladbach’s senior side midway through last season and became the club’s youngest-ever goalscorer against Bayern Munich in March of this year.

He has since developed into an increasingly influential player under head coach Alexander Blessin this term, featuring in all 10 Bundesliga matches as well as two DFB-Pokal games.

Mohya became the fourth youngest-player in Bundesliga history to score in consecutive games in October, contributing with a goal and an assist in a standout display in a 3-2 win against Stuttgart.

The dynamic and versatile attacker, who is comfortable operating centrally or out wide, has produced several impressive performances that have subsequently caught the eye of some of Europe’s biggest clubs.

According to TEAMtalk, Andoni Iraola’s Liverpool have shown concrete interest in Mohya and have intensively scouted the teenager.

The report adds the Reds are ‘ready to battle’ with high-flying Brighton & Hove Albion, who currently sit second in the Premier League table and have also been closely monitoring the attacker.

Bundesliga giants Bayern Munich, Borussia Dortmund, Bayer Leverkusen and RB Leipzig are also said to be keeping an eye on Mohya’s progress, while Real Madrid, Barcelona and AC Milan are some of the big clubs abroad who have recently entered the race for his signature.

The youngster is viewed as a key part of Monchengladbach’s plans for this season, and it is understood that an offer in the region of €45m (£37.7m) is what it would take to persuade the German club to open talks over a possible sale in the coming transfer windows.

#1641. Torreense vs Celtic - prediction, team news, lineups

By Ellis Stevens | 24 Nov 2026 12:23

Torreense welcome Celtic to Estadio Municipal de Leiria on Thursday night for a matchday five clash in the league phase of the Europa League.

The hosts are 19th in the standings with six points from four games, while the visitors are 32nd with three points after four matches.

Torreense made history by defeating Sporting Lisbon 2-1 in the Taca de Portugal final last season, marking the club's first major trophy and securing their qualification to the Europa League.

Torreense, as a result, became the first non-top flight club to qualify for the revamped league phase of the competition, and Azul-grenas have performed admirably in their opening four fixtures.

Thursday's hosts have secured two wins and suffered two defeats in their first four games, leaving Torreense placed 19th in the league phase table and on course to qualify for the knockouts.

The latest of those victories, a dramatic 3-2 win against Ararat-Armenia that featured two goals in stoppage time to come from 2-1 down to secure the win, came under new boss Joao Nuno, who was appointed after Luis Miguel Valado Tralhao mutually agreed to step down as manager.

Nuno recorded one win and one draw in his first two games, but the manager has since suffered back-to-back defeats heading into this match, leaving Torreense eager to avoid enduring a third consecutive loss.

Torreense will draw confidence from their impressive displays in the Europa League, while visitors Celtic have shown signs of weakness in this competition this term.

The Bhoys have won only one of their four league phase fixtures, alongside three defeats, scoring just six goals and conceding a considerable 11 goals in that time.

Martin O'Neill's side actually lost each of their first three league phase fixtures, results that coincided with a miserable run across all competitions, during which they recorded six defeats, one draw and just three wins between mid-September and the beginning of November.

However, a 3-2 triumph over Besiktas on matchday four of the league phase, featuring an 87th-minute winner from Camilo Duran, has sparked a three-game winning run, subsequently defeating both Kilmarnock (1-0) and St Mirren (4-1).

Celtic will be looking to extend that winning streak and secure just their second win of the league phase on Thursday, with the Bhoys hoping to move closer to the qualification places.

While Celtic have returned to winning ways in recent matches, concerns remain about their form on the road, having lost three of their last five away fixtures across all competitions.

Torreense will be without Jorge Aguirre for Thursday's fixture after the forward was sent off in the matchday four clash with Ararat-Armenia, and Adama Baradji is also not expected to feature due to an injury concern.

In Aguirre's absence, Musa Drammeh, who scored in the defeat to Benfica last time out, should lead the line, with Carlos Reina providing support in attacking midfield.

Meanwhile, Duran, who has scored 14 goals in 22 appearances for Celtic this season, should lead the line, with Sebastian Tounekti, Benjamin Nygren and Haissem Hassan providing attacking support.

Further back, Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain and Callum McGregor could feature at the base of midfield, with Cameron Carter-Vickers and Liam Scales in central defence.

AC Milan produced their best attacking display of the season on Sunday night as they put five goals past Frosinone at San Siro.

An own-goal from Gabriele Calvani early on set the tone, with Goncalo Ramos, Ardon Jashari, Alphadjo Cisse and Christian Pulisic all netting in the rout. The ruthless counter-attacking display moves Milan back inside the top four, after wins from Como, Roma and Lazio earlier in the round.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The match stats make for interesting reading. Milan edged possession with 54%, generating 2.50 Expected Goals – so scoring double what they created – but also having five big chances which matches the number of goals scored.

Frosinone remarkably had more shots in total (15 to 12), but they were more wasteful with only three on target to the Rossoneri’s eight. The visitors also racked up nine corners, the most Milan have conceded all season.

📊 The stats from the win against Frosinone. pic.twitter.com/ERVTj98m9Y

— MilanData📊 (@acmilandata) November 22, 2026

Only Nereo Rocco’s (29) and Lajos Czeizler’s (31) Milan sides scored more goals than Ruben Amorim’s (28) in their first 12 matches in charge in Serie A.

Adrien Rabiot is the first Milan midfielder to be involved in at least one goal (including goals and assists) in seven consecutive Serie A appearances since Kaká in 2004, and he became the first midfielder in the last 20 years of Serie A with more than 10 goals in his first 10 games in a single season.

With his sixth goal in his 10th Serie A appearance for Milan at 20 years and 31 days, Alphadjo Cisse became the second-youngest Rossoneri player to reach this milestone in his first 10 appearances in the three-points-for-a-win era, after Alexandre Pato , who achieved it at 18 years and 189 days.

No team has scored more goals than Milan in the first 15 minutes of play in the five major European leagues currently underway (7, like Barcelona and Chelsea).

Milan are now unbeaten in all seven meetings against Frosinone in Serie A (W5 D2): among the teams against which they have never lost in the competition, the Rossoneri have played more games only against Pisa (14 – six also against Crotone and Lecco).

Milan have won five of their last six league games (L1), scoring at least two goals in each, after failing to win three of their previous four (D3). The last time they scored more than one goal in a run of Serie A matches was between September 2020 and January 2021, when they managed 15 games.

#1639. Chelsea news: £75m player seriously considered retirement under Enzo Maresca

By Oliver Thomas | 24 Nov 2026 12:42

Chelsea defender Wesley Fofana has admitted that he seriously considered retiring from football during Enzo Maresca’s time in charge at Stamford Bridge.

The one-cap France international joined the West Londoners from Leicester City for a reported £75m in the summer of 2022 and has since played 81 times for the club across all competitions.

Fofana’s career at Chelsea has largely been disrupted by injury, missing a total of 41 matches during Maresca’s 18-month reign with the Blues.

While Fofana began the 2024-25 season fit after recovering from a year-long ACL tear, two major hamstring injuries wiped out nearly six months of his campaign.

The 25-year-old centre-back has since opened up about how the psychological strain that came with a rash of injuries almost led to the decision to prematurely call time on his career.

Speaking in an interview for Zack Nani TV, as quoted by the Evening Standard, Fofana said: “There was a period when I was recovering from my cruciate ligament and meniscus injuries.

“Then I suffered two consecutive hamstring strains under Enzo Maresca, when I really decided: ‘That’s it, I’m retiring, I’m done playing.’ I was serious.

“I really wanted to stop, because, for the first time in my life, I wasn’t happy anymore. It wasn’t just about being injured or not playing; my whole life was completely shattered. I wasn’t myself anymore. I sincerely believed that, in the future, I would only get injured.

“I thought to myself: ‘That’s it, football isn’t for me, I’m too fragile.’ I even used Abou Diaby as an example. I thought to myself: ’I guess I’m the Abou Diaby of our generation. There has to be someone like that, and it happened to me. It’s my destiny, I accept it.’”

Fofana added: “Of course, I was very sad and didn’t want to stop, because I was living my dream. At that point, I called my agents so we could sit down and talk, telling them, ‘Okay, I’ve decided to retire.’

“They started analysing the situation with me, talking about contracts and all that: ‘It’s simple, you still have several years left on your contract, and there’s a lot of money to be made.

“Even if you really decide to stop playing, you still have to come every day, keep smiling, and even if you’re injured, you have to honour your contract for your future.’

“But at that moment, I really felt that the pain football caused me far outweighed the joy, so why continue? I was in pain almost 100 per cent of the time.

“Every time I gritted my teeth, played a few games, and just started to find a little love and joy in life again, bang, I’d get injured again.”

Fofana has since made positive progress in building up his strength and fitness; he played 38 times for Chelsea in all competitions last season and has started seven of the first 11 Premier League matches under new manager Xabi Alonso so far this term.

Last month, Alonso publicly backed Fofana as an "important," "focused," and "mature" first-team figure, who is under contract at Stamford Bridge until the summer of 2029.

#1638. Report: Liverpool transfer blow could lead to surprise January deal

Liverpool's recruitment drive looks set to continue this winter.

The Reds have spent over £650 million since winning the Premier League in 2025, but the rebuild is far from complete.

Julian Ward has taken the reigns within the Anfield recruitment team and work is now being done to action some of the club's winter plans.

Andoni Iraola's side aren't the only team looking to do business in January though, and a European giant could spoil the plans of the Merseyside club.

The potential transfer blow would frustrate Liverpool but could open the door for another deal to be completed sooner than planned.

Barcelona join race for Liverpool targetThe Reds are in the market for defensive reinforcements, and VfB Stuttgart standout Finn Jeltsch has been one of the most exciting names linked with a Merseyside move. The Reds are in the market for defensive reinforcements, and VfB Stuttgart standout Finn Jeltsch has been one of the most exciting names linked with a Merseyside move.

Liverpool are one of many top European clubs monitoring the 20-year-old German defender, who has played in every Bundesliga game for Stuttgart so far this season.

Several top sides are already in the race for Jeltsch's signature, but La Liga leaders Barcelona have now identified the wonderkid as a target.

That's according to an update from Ekrem Konur, who claims that Barca now consider Jeltsch a potential defensive option, with Hansi Flick an admirer of the youngster's profile.

Arsenal, Inter Milan and Manchester United are all named alongside Liverpool as potential rivals for Jeltsch's signature, but Barcelona winning the race could actually do the Reds a favour.

The Reds have a buy option, but there is uncertainty around whether they will be willing to pay the full amount.

If Barcelona were to make a winter move for Jeltsch then the door could open for Liverpool to negotiate a cheaper option for Araujo in January.

Ward will hope that he can be the man to win the race for Jeltsch, but if Liverpool don't sign the 20-year-old then a move to Barcelona could be a boost for the Reds too.

#1637. Pandur hails Rangers legend for showing him the ropes at Ibrox

Published: 15:33 EST, 20 November 2026 | Updated: 15:36 EST, 20 November 2026

Rangers goalkeeper Ivor Pandur has revealed his 'unbelievable' experience of working under Allan McGregor.

The former Rangers, Hull and Scotland keeper was brought into the Ibrox backroom staff by Derek McInnes as lead goalkeeping coach in the summer.

Pandur is reaping the benefits of his mentor’s experience and their relationship having kept eight clean sheets during his team’s 12-match unbeaten run.

'It’s unbelievable,' said the Croatian ahead of the Premiership encounter at Motherwell on Saturday night.

'With the career that he had here, he obviously has a lot of experience.

'We have a great relationship where he is my coach, he is my friend. So he’ll tell me when I ask him if I can do something better.

Ivor Pandur has made an impressive start to life at Rangers after joining from Hull City

'We are here to make each other better. If I can make him a better coach, that’s brilliant. But he’s making me a better goalkeeper and I’m really, really thankful for that.

'Training, first of all, is really, really enjoyable. And he always asks, "What do I want to do? What do I want to improve?". And he’ll give me feedback.

'There’s not a single thing, I would say, that made me better. Just in general, to be able to work in these kind of circumstances and conditions, it’s really enjoyable and it’s making me happy every day.

'It’s making me excited to come to work. And that’s because of him also.

'He’s a great guy and he was a great goalkeeper, and it’s enough for me to learn from.'

Manager McInnes this week described Pandur as a key 'driver' of team culture off the pitch, citing the respect he has from his team-mates.

Pandur, who joined from Hull in the summer, said: 'I always want to lead by example. The words are not so important if you’re not doing your job right.

'So if I can lead by example and show up every day, work as hard as I can, a lot of young players can see that.

Pandur insists he is only going to keep improving under the guidance of Allan McGregor

'And obviously, I’m always there to help somebody. I was also 19 or 20 and, when I had somebody to learn from, it was much easier.

'Because you get experiences through life and through years of playing, I always try to help everybody else.

'So there are times where I can be more vocal if I feel a need for it, but it’s never my first objective. It’s always to lead by example.'

Pandur is still awaiting his first international cap but was again away with Croatia this month and he feels meeting the demands of Rangers fans is getting the best out of him.

'It keeps you on your toes,” the former Rijeka, Hellas Verona and Fortuna Sittard player said. 'But in my opinion, pressure is in your head.

'We all play the game we love and we try to do our best. Some days you’ll do good, some days you’ll do bad. We always try to do the right thing.

'Pressure is bigger here, there’s more followers. But it can only make you better because it gets everything out of you.'

#1634. OFI Crete vs Anderlecht - prediction, team news, lineups

By Matt Law | 24 Nov 2026 12:49, Last updated: 24 Nov 2026 12:52

Anderlecht will be aiming to make it three straight wins in the league stage of the Europa League when they travel to OFI Crete on Thursday night.

The visitors will bring a four-game unbeaten run in all competitions into this match, but Crete will enter the European fixture off the back of a 2-0 loss to Panathinaikos in the Greek Super League.

OFI have a record of two wins and two losses from their four matches in the league stage of this season's Europa League, with six points leaving them in 16th position in the overall table.

The Club started their league phase with a 2-0 win over Hoffenheim before losing back-to-back games in the competition against Rennes and Bayer Leverkusen.

However, Christos Kontis' side posted a 2-0 victory over H. Beer Sheva in their last Europa League game on November 5, so they will be aiming to make it back-to-back wins in the tournament.

OFI are playing in the league stage/group stage of a major European tournament for the first time since the 1995-96 campaign, and this is also the first time that they have ever qualified for this round of the UEFA Cup/Europa League.

The Club have European matches to come against Benfica, Sturm Graz and Lech before the end of the group stage in early 2027.

Anderlecht, meanwhile, have also won two and lost two of their four matches in this season's Europa League league stage, with six points leaving them 15th in the table.

The Belgian club started their league phase with a 2-1 loss to Lyon, before going down 1-0 to Dinamo Zagreb in the middle of October, but they have won their last two matches in the tournament against Jagiellonia and Red Bull Salzburg to move onto six points.

Vitor Bruno's side will enter this match off the back of a 1-0 win over Leuven in the league, with the result leaving them in fifth position in Belgium's top flight.

Anderlecht will face Hoffenheim, Sunderland and Marseille in their three European matches after this one, and it would be a surprise if they were not present in the knockout round.

The Purple and Whites won this competition back in 1982-83, and this is their first Europa League league phase campaign since 2024-25.

Crete will be without the services of Kenan Kodro, Kresimir Krizmanic, Fotis Koutsoupias, Konstantinos Lagoudakis, Emmanouil Chnaris and Nikos Marinakis due to injury problems.

Taxiarchis Fountas has scored five times in 19 appearances this season, and the 31-year-old is set to feature in the final third of the field for the hosts.

Meanwhile, there should also be a position in the side for Thiago Nuss, who has provided seven goal contributions in all competitions for Crete this term.

As for Anderlecht, Ilay Camara and Lucas Hey are out of the match due to injury problems.

Mihajlo Cvetkovic has been in strong form for his Belgian club this season, scoring seven goals and registering two assists in 22 matches, and the 19-year-old will continue in the final third of the field.

There are also expected to be spots in the final third for Danylo Sikan and Jayden Onia-Seke.

Lilo; Shielis, Nikolaou, Poungouras; Dickmann, Bouchalakis, Androutsos, Athanasiou; Cantalapiedra, Nuss, Fountas

Coosemans; Maamar, Omobamidele, Petrot, Augustinsson; Ambros, Llansana, Stroeykens, Onia-Seke; Sikan, Cvetkovic

This is a difficult match to call; cases can be made for either side to pick up all three points, but we are expecting a close fixture to end with the points being shared.

#1633. Report: Liverpool take first step to sign new Florian Wirtz, they want him badly

Liverpool have reportedly taken their first step towards signing the next Florian Wirtz. The German could already have a successor.

Florian Wirtz enjoyed a magnificent day against Manchester United on Sunday. The no.7 lit up Anfield with an incredible performance, creating 10 chances (five considered 'big') and scoring himself.

It was the Wirtz show and demonstrated why Liverpool bought him in the first place. Yes, it's a shame we've had to wait well over a year to actually see why but this has been a long time coming.

Wirtz has not played poorly. Things have rarely gone his way, though, and this dysfunctional Liverpool team hasn't made it easy for a player who relies on finding space and having runners beyond him.

When he gets that space and gets those runners, though, Wirtz tears teams apart. As he did against United - they had no idea how to cope with him and that was evident with 11, let alone 10.

But there's always been an extra problem with focusing the team around Wirtz - there's only one of him. Liverpool don't have another natural playmaker who can operate behind a striker but they need one if they're to go all-out on building around the position.

The next Florian WirtzThere are always wonderkids coming through in the Bundesliga who catch they eye. Few reached Wirtz's level, admittedly, but it's a fantastic league for young attacking talent to thrive in. And that's caught Liverpool's eye, it seems. Christian Falk claims they've now got a 'concrete' interest in Wael Mohya, who is lighting the Bundesliga up for Borussia Mönchengladbach.

There are always wonderkids coming through in the Bundesliga who catch they eye. Few reached Wirtz's level, admittedly, but it's a fantastic league for young attacking talent to thrive in.

And that's caught Liverpool's eye, it seems. Christian Falk claims they've now got a 'concrete' interest in Wael Mohya, who is lighting the Bundesliga up for Borussia Mönchengladbach.

Jürgen Klopp actually had a look at Mohya for Germany in the latest international break - a massive show of faith in the 17-year-old, even if he didn't make his debut. But it feels as though it's just a matter of time before he's in that senior team.

And maybe in Liverpool's, too. They view Mohya as potential backup for Wirtz, as well as long-term competition for the player. They're not alone in their pursuit, mind, as Brighton would also like to make him their latest young gamble.

We imagine Mohya will cost a fortune for an 18-year-old next year, though it won't be in January. Gladbach are trying to tie him down to a new deal and refuse to sell in the winter window - so it'll be the summer at the earliest if Liverpool are to get ahold of him.

Bayer Leverkusen and Bayern Munich are both keen admirers as well, meaning the price here could actually get out of hand. But Liverpool are fans and certainly want a player in that position. They'll just be tested for how much they want that player to be Mohya.

#1632. Andoni Iraola: Liverpool cannot ‘sustain the level’ I want

Andoni Iraola has conceded that Liverpool cannot currently “sustain the level” he expects after his side squandered a two-goal lead for the second match in a row.

In the Spaniard’s first game at Anfield since becoming manager, Monaco fought back to win 3-2 by virtue of Paris Brunner’s late glancing header seven days on from Leeds United’s 4-2 victory in Chicago, emphasising Liverpool’s alarming lack of depth, particularly in defence.

“We played a good first half, especially a good 30 minutes. Right now we probably don’t have much more, in terms of the levels required to play like this. They deserved to turn around the game.

“We won the first two pre-season games, but the last two we cannot sustain the level we want for all of the game. As soon as we made some changes, players start to get tired and we cannot sustain that level. So, we have work to do.”

Alex on target 🎯 pic.twitter.com/PT6AYrLxyz

Alisson, Virgil van Dijk and Cody Gakpo all made their first appearances and contributed to a lively first-half in which Iraola’s commitment to man-to-man marking and an intensive pressing structure were evident out of possession. With the ball in the first half they demonstrated the kind of slick passing that Bournemouth employed to carve opponents open on the counter-attack.

A nimble one-two between Ryan Gravenberch and Dominik Szoboszlai allowed the Dutch midfielder to set up Alexander Isak to score with a shot from 16 yards and the most expensive player in English football history laid claim to the second, too, when he seemed to hook in a rebound from Lukas Hradecky’s save while lying in the six-yard box.

Later he would graciously acknowledge that he and Florian Wirtz had connected with the ball simultaneously and he was happy to yield the credit to his team-mate.

Our second goal of the game, scored by Wirtz… we think 🤔 pic.twitter.com/FUzA363Oxw

At that point it seemed that victory would be a cakewalk but just before half-time Aleksandr Golovin caught Van Dijk out with a feint and late swerve to the right, tripping over the Liverpool captain’s clumsy hack. Despite a heavy limp, Golovin hammered the penalty past Alisson’s dive to make it 2-1 at the break.

Iraola rationed his early changes at the start of the second half to two but Liverpool could not regain their rhythm and Mika Biereth capitalised on a Gravenberch error to score the equaliser after battling to be first to the rebound when Giorgi Mamardashvili saved his first effort, stroking his effort through Wataru Endo’s legs.

Cue five substitutions as soon as that goal had gone in and a raft more followed, killing the remaining half-hour of all momentum and cohesion. By the time Brunner exploited a dozy mix-up between Milos Kerkez and Federico Chiesa about whose responsibility he was at a corner to flash his header past Mamardashvili, only two of the 22 starters were still on the pitch.

Liverpool: Alisson (Mamardashvili 46), Tsimikas (Kerkez 59), Van Dijk (c) (Chambers 59), Ndukwe (Endo 46), Frimpong (Ramsay 75), Gravenberch (Nyoni 59), Gakpo (Ngumoha 59), Wirtz (McConnell 59), Koumas (Chiesa 75), Isak (Muñoz 59)Substitutes: Morrison, Davies.Goals: Isak (16), Wirtz (29)Monaco: Hradecky, Nazinho (Mawissa 75), Dier (c) (Kehrer 75), S Sané, Vanderson (Teze 46), Golovin (Idumbo 75), Cabral (Soubeir 75), Camara (Benzahra 64), Detourbet (Coulibaly 64), Biereth (Brunner 80), Abline (Konaté 64).Substitutes: Assab, Kohn, Lienard, Nibombe, Touré.  Goals: Golovin (44 pen), Biereth (56), Brunner (88)

They played well in the first half, as they did against Leeds, but lost all shape and structure in the second half to lose 3-2.

Yellow card for Konate for clattering into Endo late. That’s the last of the action.

Liverpool 2 Monaco 3 (Brunner)  Brilliant near-post glancing header from a devilishly whippy, dipping corner. Kerkez doing his best Rip van Winkle impression.

Diligent defensive work by Ngumoha stops Konate’s run down the outside left.

A final substitution, hopefully. Brunner replaces Biereth. Konate’s shot, a pearoller, is easily saved by Mamardashvili after A mix-up between Kerkez and Munoz.

As usual, the substitutions have killed the game. Watched Leeds vs RB Leipzig yesterday. They played two 60 minute matches which kept it more competitive for longer but still descended into a kickabout late on.

Mawissa, Kehrer, Idumbo and Soubeir have replaced Nazinho, Dier, Golovin and Cabral.

Monaco also made changes, four I think. Will catch up with then once they’re confirmed. Ramsey is into the game straight away tp stop Coulibaly’s shot.

Ramsay, Chiesa and Elliott are coming on for Szoboszlai, Frimpong and Koumas. Lovely applause for Elliott.

Konate sweeps a left-foot shot from the left of the box past the right post with Mamardashvili forced into a headlong dive. Liverpool have lost their defensive shape and intensity, allowing Monaco to punch holes through the lines with some direct running.

Nazinho gets round Frimpong down the Monaco left and cuts back the perfect pass to put it on a plate for Coulibaly who hammers a left-foot shot from the right of the D that Mamardashvili throws up his hands to block. That would have stung. Good save. A flag would have meant it wouldn’t have counted but even so Frimpong’s defensive work wasn’t good enough.

It’s been very scrappy since the changes but then Ngumoha pounces on to a loose ball, glides up the right and tries to play Koumas in behind the back four. Sadly, he overhits the pass which trickles out for a goal-kick. Cue an ovation and cries of ‘Rio! Rio!’

Three changes for Monaco with Detoubet, Abline and Camara departing for Benzhara, Coulibaly and Konaté.

Ngumoha has gone to the right wing and Koumas is playing through the middle as a false nine.

Liverpool make five changes with Gakpo, Van Dijk, Wirtz, Tsimikas and Isak departing while Munoz makes his ‘debut’ with Ngumoha, Nyoni, Chambers, McConell and Kerkez.

Liverpool 2 Monaco 2 (Biereth) Mistake by Gravenberch allows Golovin to play a pass into the left half of the box for Biereth. His first shot is well saved by Mamardashvili at full stretch but his tenacity allowed him to get to the rebound ahead of Endo, swivel and stick his second effort in to equalise.

Monaco overplay at the edge of the box, Detourbet, Biereth and Abline playing ‘after you. Claud’, instead of shooting.

A slick, short passing move between Gravenberch, Wirtz and Isak ends with Isak on the deck in the box after Gravenberch’s step-over allowed the ball to run to him. Isak took a touch to move the ball on to his left but gave the defender a glimmer of it and he hacked it away before felling Isak as well as collateral damage.

Quiet start to the half. Biereth just pressed Mamardashvili but the keeper managed to sweep the ball away even though under more pressure than he would have expected.

Liverpool try to play out from the back with Mamardashvili spearing a straight pass to Gravenberch who tried to knock it round the corner for Endo but the ball skidded under his studs and out for a throw-in.

Isak is apparently claiming both goals. Replays are indistinct. He could have clipped it in off his heel as he had a swing at the ball while grounded at the same time as Wirtz.

Our second goal of the game, scored by Wirtz… we think 🤔 pic.twitter.com/FUzA363Oxw

Endo has slotted in at centre-back alongside Van Dijk.

Half-time changes: Mamardashvili for Alisson and Endo for Ndukwe.

For Monaco, Teze for Vanderson at right-back.

Much to admire in that first-half performance from Liverpool’s front six and centre-backs, the latter two particularly out of possession and winning it back. The man-to-man system is working well for them. But they should be out of sight by now instead of leading by only a goal.

Liverpool free-kick on the right after a foul on Koumas. Szoboszlai whips in the cross and Van Dijk gets up first to the left of the penalty spot but bludgeons his header about a foot wide of the right post.

Charlie Adam says the penalty was ‘a soft one’ but Van Dijk did not adjust when Golovin shifted it to his right, stuck out a leg and Golovim understandably decided to topple over the hurdle.

Liverpool 2 Monaco 1 (Golovin, pen) Speared it into the top right. Alisson went the right way but was beaten for pace and power.

The referee, Jarred Gillett, gives Monaco a penalty. It was deserved, too. Golovin went on a driving run down the middle, shifted it to his right and was tripped by Van Dijk.

Liverpool are well worth their lead. They are streets ahead of Monaco.

A microcosm of the game so far: Liverpool pass goes astray, a player wins it back – this time Gakpo – by snapping into a tackle before laying it off to his left for the unmarked Tsimikas to skim a low shot about a foot wide of the left post from 25 yards.

Monaco have done very little since that wee salvo in the opening minute but just now Abline was given too much space from distance but whacked his shot into the Kop.

Big cheer from the crowd for Hugo Ekitike

The impressive Koumas diddles Nazinho with a Cruyff turn but then thumps his shot straight into Hradecky’s chest.

Liverpool 2 Monaco 0 (Wirtz) Pass chipped out to Koumas down the right who arcs a cross to the back post. Gakpo meets it with a header back across goal to Isak whose first effort from a couple of yards is blocked but the ball gets stuck under Isak’s falling body and Wirtz is Johnny on the Spot to stab it in from a 18 inches as Dier tried to scramble it away.

Liverpool have been impressive so far but if there has been a weakness it’s still the balance in central midfield defensively. Going forward both Gravenberch and Szobiszlai have dovetailed together well. They win the ball back when Van Dijk steps out and the midfield two fly forward to tee up Koumas for a shot that strikes Dier.

Chance for Wirtz, who opens his body from the left of the D to try to bend a shot into the bottom right corner but fizzes it the wrong side of the post.

It’s been pretty breathless since the goal, Liverpool dozily letting Monaco through the middle before twice cutting Monaco apart in midfield only for Isak to overrun a pass in the box delivered by Wirtz and then Koumas to shoot over.

Liverpool 1 Monaco 0 (Isak) Chip to Gakpo down the left of the box, he clips it first time back to Gravenberch in the D who lays it off to Szoboszlai. Ping-ping-ping. Szoboszlai keeps the tempo high with return, the one in the one-two with Gravenberch who picks out Isak to bury a shot from about 15 yards into the bottom left corner.

Alex on target 🎯 pic.twitter.com/PT6AYrLxyz

Excellent move from Liverpool, instigated by Ndukwe’s fine tackle on Biereth. He knocks it short to Gravenberch who arrows a 60-yard pass out to Koumas hurtling down the right. He measures his cross perfectly for Gakpo stealing in off the left wing and though he connects powerfully with the meat of his brow, he bashes it straight at the keeper. He was offside in any case, it transpires.

Charlie Adam on co-comms points out that Liverpool are going man-to-man now in classic Iraola/Bielsa style and when the camera goes high you can see it, especially with the full-backs.

Liverpool are carving the middle of the park up with incisive passing. Szoboszlai starts a move that sends Isak down the left of the box. He traps the chip, turns back to face away from goal and taps a pass back to Wirtz who gallops on to it and bends a shot that Hradecky dives low to his left to beat away with a firm left wrist. Frimpong pounces on the rebound and clips a tame effort straight at Hradecky who had quickly restored himself to the vertical.

Van Dijk gobbles up a long pass over Ndukwe, snuffing out any possibility of Biereth getting there first.

Tsimikas is free down the left but overhits his cross on the run when Isak was begging for a cut-back. The left-back went for the back post and ballooned his centre behind, miles beyond Koumas and Wirtz.

Liverpool defend the corner solidly and Frimpong races away on the counter, bombing on to the ball and sprinting into the Monaco half. But his touch is not as sound as his pace and Monaco deal with him when he fluffs his control.

A period of applause in memory of Kevin Keegan ❤️ pic.twitter.com/AkPZG7babe

Liverpool kick off defending the Kop. They roll the ball back to Frimpong who chips a long pass up the right to Koumas who hares on to the pass down the right and crosses, just beyond Isak. Hradecky gathers and bowls the ball out. A mistake by Tisimikas lets Biereth barrel through the inside-right to hammer a shot that Alisson turns behind for a corner.

The crowd applauds in the modern way. My goodness he was a terrific player. Saw him play for Liverpool, Southampton and Newcastle. Absolutely relentless.

Virgil van Dijk has the pennant. Liverpool are wearing all red with the paint splashes of the 1990 kit. Monaco are in a very pale green.

For me it’s a special game, most of the players and people will be ‘it’s [just] a pre-season friendly’, but for me it’s a lot more than this. It will be the first time I have the chance to go out, to feel this stadium and I hope we can also perform well.

It’s a good game for us, because it’s going to be demanding, it’s a team that wants to dominate and they also want to press high so we will see how we are.

I think the cases of Ali[sson], Cody, and Virgil I think it’s their first game. It shouldn’t go longer than 45 minutes, maybe a little bit more if they feel comfortable.

Also for some of the others Ryan, Flo, and Alex, it’s the second game so we have to be aware of those things.

But the league starts in two weeks, so we cannot wait also too much; we have to give them quality minutes.

I think today is going to be a good reference, two games – Monaco and Como – teams that try dominate the game, they are very good in possession, so they will demand us the best without the ball. If we want to control the game and also physical teams, they are probably a very good test.

I hope we are at the level and we can do very good games.

Liverpool Alisson; Frimpong, Ndukwe, Van Dijk, Tsimikas; Szoboszlai, Gakpo; Koumaz, Wirtz, Gakpo; Isak.

Monaco Hradecky; Vanderson, Dier, Sané, Nazinho; Detourbet, Cabral, Camara, Golovin, Abline, Biereth.

Le 𝐗𝐈 qui débutera cette rencontre face à 𝐋𝐢𝐯𝐞𝐫𝐩𝐨𝐨𝐥 📋 pic.twitter.com/2cOYRbzUEN

🥳 Feliz aniversário, 𝐅𝐢𝐥𝐢𝐩𝐞 𝐋𝐮𝐢́𝐬! 🎉Notre coach fête aujourd'hui ses 41 ans 🎂 pic.twitter.com/VTd4BQ5rRK

Alisson, Van Dijk and Gakpo return, Ndukwe continues in defence.

The Reds to take on AS Monaco at Anfield!Watch the match LIVE on All Red Video 📺

Good afternoon and welcome to live coverage of the first of two Liverpool home friendlies after their preseason tour of the United States. Andoni Iraola’s side saw off Wrexham and Sunderland in their first two matches but gave away a two-goal lead at half-time in the final fixture and ended up being beaten 4-2 by Leeds United in Chicago in the last game after multiple changes. What did we learn? Not a huge amount in the absence of Virgil van Dijk, Alisson, Víctor Muñoz, Cody Gakpo and Alexis Mac Allister, the first four of whom are available today other than an ongoing vulnerability from set-pieces and Curtis Jones looking like he is in desperate need of a fresh start.

This afternoon at Anfield they take on AS Monaco who finished seventh in Ligue 1 this season but are under new management with the recruitment of the former Chelsea and Atlético left-back Filipe Luís as head coach. It’s quite the coup for Le Rocher given he led Flamengo to their first Brazilian title in five years, the Copa Libertadores and the Copa do Brasil in his 18 months in charge.

In pre-season so far he has overseen a 5-2 win over fourth-tier AS Saint-Priest, a 2-0 defeat by Sporting Clube, a 2-2 draw with Cercle Bruges and a 1-0 victory over Getafe. They have sold their best player, Maghnes Akliouche, to PSG for £43m and Aladji Bamba to Newcastle for £34m but have so far retained Mamadou Coulibaly and Folarin Balogun, signed and made Ansu Fati’s loan move into a long-term deal.

Iraola may well persevere with Trey Nyoni in midfield who, after his performances on tour, ought to be on the threshold of a breakthrough season and it would be interesting to see him paired with Ryan Gravenberch just behind Dominik Szoboszlai.

Ifeanyi Ndukwe, who played well in America after coming on for the injured Joe Gomez, does not have a UK work permit and will have to go abroad on loan for the season but Jérémy Jacquet, who has yet to feature, was due to have a fitness test this morning and would be a welcome to boost to a squad whose defence still requires significant reinforcements.

#1631. “Annoyed” Kevin De Bruyne faces uncertain Napoli future ahead of Man City return

By Oliver Thomas | 24 Nov 2026 13:05

Manchester City legend Kevin De Bruyne is preparing for an emotional homecoming at the Etihad Stadium on Tuesday night, though his current spell with Napoli has been clouded by transfer speculation and internal friction.

After winning 19 trophies during a glittering 10-year career at Man City, the 35-year-old playmaker reluctantly left the club at the end of the 2024-25 season when the decision was made to not extend his contract.

De Bruyne subsequently signed for Napoli as a free agent, embarking on a fresh challenge in Italian football, but his debut campaign was struck by injury, starting only 16 matches across all competitions as Napoli surrendered their Serie A crown to Inter Milan.

The Belgium international has since played in all 16 games for Napoli across Serie A and the Champions League this term, chipping in with four goals and two assists while operating in a deeper midfield position under head coach Massimiliano Allegri.

De Bruyne is part of an aging Napoli side that are currently languishing down in eighth place in Serie A and sit 27th in the Champions League standings after losing three of their opening four League Phase games.

Tensions boiled over during Napoli’s heavy 4-1 UCL loss at Porto earlier this month, where teammates had to separate De Bruyne and striker Lorenzo Lucca following an angry on-pitch row.

"Speaking about the pitch, De Bruyne is the best player this year at Napoli. The point is that the whole team is having difficulties, Naples-based journalist Vincenzo Credendino told BBC Sport.

"We saw that there is a problem, at least between De Bruyne and Lorenzo Lucca. Their acting was very, very clear and I think that in that time, the two of them were wrong.

"On one hand you cannot swear at another team-mate but on the other hand, De Bruyne reproached Lucca without encouraging him, so it was a bad show."

As De Bruyne enters the twilight years of his career, it has been suggested that the “spark never really ignited” between the midfielder and the Naples outfit, raising uncertainty over his future at the club.

When asked about his future at a press conference ahead of Napoli’s Champions League clash with Man City, De Bruyne said: "Not a lot I can say for the moment. I have played at 100% until now and obviously I am not 20 years old, I am turning 36.

"There is a lot of things going in my mind but there is not a lot to say. I am playing good football, trying to help the team to do well and it has been a bit of a challenging season with a lot of things happening."

De Bruyne will soon be entering the final six months of his Napoli contract and will be free to negotiate pre-contract agreements with foreign clubs in January.

De Bruyne has also expressed his annoyance over the backlash he and his family have received following controversial comments made by the player’s wife in September.

His wife Michele reportedly told Belgian magazine NINA about their desire to move back to Belgium, saying "the sooner we get there, the better" as De Bruyne leads a "very restricted life" in Naples.

Addressing the media fallout, De Bruyne replied: "To be honest, I am pretty annoyed because if you read the article, that none of you have read, to understand what she said.

"I was away in Belgium and a lot of noise came and a lot of bad reactions to my wife and family. I saw pictures of my house, I don't think it is OK but it is what it is and some press created this in Italy. I don't know why.

"Nobody knows my life, you will never know. People who work with me are not allowed to say anything but obviously it is something that I take away and think about. It has not been nice for my wife or for my family."

De Bruyne has since been linked with a sensational Premier League return in January, while Dutch giants PSV Eindhoven are understood to have failed with a €2m (£1.7m) opening offer to sign him in the New Year, with Napoli valuing the midfielder closer to €8m (£6.7m), according to Credendino.

Napoli boss Allegri has interestingly refused to rule out a mid-season departure for De Bruyne, stating on Monday that transfer decisions are "down to the players and who wants to leave" once January arrives.

Meanwhile, De Bruyne has spoken out for the first time since Man City were found guilty of breaching Premier League financial regulations.

#1630. Amorim explains dislike for ‘AmorimBall’ term and what leaves him ‘really worried’ about Milan

Ruben Amorim had some interesting comments after the Frosinone win, including why he is not a fan of a term that is going viral.

Milan put on a five-star display at San Siro on Sunday night as they routed that Canarini. All five of their goals came via flowing counter-attacks, which has led to the tag ‘AmorimBall’ doing the rounds on social media, with many believing things are starting to truly click.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The head coach is keeping his feet firmly on the ground though, as he spoke after the game about the need to find consistency both within matches but also from game-to-game. In this sense, Thursday’s trip to face Olympiacos is another big test.

Amorim was present in the press conference room at San Siro following the win to answer questions from journalists, with his comments relayed by MilanNews.

“I don’t like that expression. I think we play games to win, we want to dominate the opponent. I don’t think we succeeded today: every game has its own story, and today it was man-on-man.

“Today we didn’t have to prepare much: the idea was simply to give the ball to Pulisic, to Moreira, and then exploit the combinations of these players, the understandings they already have, and conquer space.

“Today you saw that we didn’t spend much time near the opponent’s penalty area and we scored five goals, because the space wasn’t there, it was forty meters away to attack on the run.

“That’s why Cisse came on to play as a striker and not, for example, Camarda: because there was space behind him and Cisse is very good at that. So, I think we’ve played very good games in the past, but today it was just a question of the quality of the players, of one-on-ones, of reading the game.

“Today it wasn’t a question of the coach, I think, but of the players. And they, since it was man-on-man, just had to do what they can do. when they’re so good: beating the man and opening up space. So today the credit goes entirely to the players.”

“I watched the France game and I think he’s one of the best players on the team. So I think his importance is paramount. You can see there’s rotation, there’s a lot of talent. France has a lot of talent, but Rabiot is always there. There’s a reason for that.

“And then, if you look at the way France play, with Mbappé, with the way all these players position themselves on the pitch, sometimes with four players with Olise as the No. 10, he has to stay there to play a different kind of game.

“With us, he’s the player who has to push the team forward, he’s the decisive element. In France, however, he has a different job to do. So it depends more on his role in the national team and his role at Milan.

“This changes his way of interpreting the game, and it’s further proof of how Rabiot can play by adapting to the team he’s in. For me, therefore, he’s one of the best midfielders in Europe. I hope his contract renewal comes soon.”

“Today’s match wasn’t just about tactics. We saw changes in position, one-on-one situations with plenty of space: it seemed like a crazy game. What I felt against Genoa and in the other matches was that we were too far away, we didn’t reach the final third of the pitch.

“We’re not like the big teams: if you look at the big teams, like Juventus, they might struggle to get results, but you see the volume they produce. For us, it’s a bit of the opposite, so I’m really worried that, if we don’t improve, we won’t be able to maintain this number of points.

“Today, however, was a step forward: we saw many players attacking the depth, something we hadn’t seen against Ferencvaros. In the other matches, we’d managed the ball well, but today we needed pace and runs.

“We need to be able to play both games within the same game, but today was clearly the type of game we needed to win.”

#1628. Antonio Conte hits back after missing out on Man United job: Ex-Chelsea boss warns clubs they are 'frightened of winning' if they don't hire him in cryptic interview after Mauricio Pochettino landed Old Trafford gig

Published: 15:10 EST, 20 November 2026 | Updated: 15:50 EST, 20 November 2026

Antonio Conte has claimed clubs are 'frightened of winning' if they have concerns over his methods after the Italian was overlooked for the Manchester United job.

Conte had been heavily linked with the role at Old Trafford, joining Julian Nagelsmann, Eddie Howe and Unai Emery among the list bookmakers' favourites to replace Michael Carrick.

Man United ultimately went with another former Chelsea and Tottenham boss in Mauricio Pochettino, paying around £10million in compensation to lure him away from being head coach of the United States' national team.

Conte, who remains out of work after leaving Napoli in the summer, has now hit back at reports suggesting Man United may have been put off by his intensity and demands.

'First, let me address the question of my method,' Conte told the Cronache di Spogliatoio podcast.

'If anyone is frightened by my method, then they are frightened of winning, because that methodology leads to victory. That is my answer.

Antonio Conte has claimed clubs are 'frightened of winning' if they have concerns over his methods after the Italian was overlooked for the Manchester United job

Man United opted to appoint Mauricio Pochettino as head coach after sacking Michael Carrick

Conte hit back at suggestions Man United's hierachy might have been relucant to appoint him because of his methods

'Manchester United has such a significant history that I find it strange to imagine anyone could be afraid of an approach aimed at restoring the club to its true stature.

'(United) last won the league in 2013, under Ferguson. I have immense respect for Sir Alex Ferguson.

'I've read his book, and when I was in London, I was fortunate enough to visit his home and spend a day with him. He has an incredible passion for talking about football, though, at times, his Scottish accent can be quite hard to follow.

'Through his own methodology and approach, he made Manchester United great.

'That is why I find certain remarks almost offensive toward United; it's as if someone were placing a veto on the club's return to its own history.

'A method is what's needed to achieve major results. And if you're suggesting that this method requires hard work, well, yes, it does. Everyone has to work hard, not just the players.'

Conte has long been known for his combustible personality - as well as an impressive winning record as a coach.

At Chelsea, he fell out with star striker Diego Costa, centre back David Luiz and the club's board. At Napoli, he left a year after winning the Serie A title and said there was 'too much poison, too much malice' at the club.

Conte has developed a reputation for his high intensity and demands, while the Italian famously left Tottenham after an explosive press conference attacking the club's culture

Conte has won five Serie A titles across three clubs and won the Premier League with Chelsea

Conte famously left Tottenham after an explosive press conference in 2023, where he labelled his players as 'selfish' and took aim at the club's culture.

The Italian, however, has overseen five Serie A title wins during his spells at Juventus, Inter Milan and Napoli, along with winning the Premier League and FA Cup with Chelsea.

It is not the first time Conte has spoken out in recent weeks following links to Old Trafford, with the 57-year-old having denied he had set 'specific conditions' about taking over at United.

La Repubblica claimed Conte wanted 'carte blanche on the transfer market' and to act as a manager, rather than a head coach, with a technical staff behind the scenes chosen by him involving 'trusted collaborators'.

'My name has been linked with numerous clubs, but there are currently no negotiations at an advanced stage,' Conte responded on social media last month.

'Following a wonderful and successful spell in charge of Napoli, I will take the time I need to consider how and when to return to management. It will be a carefully considered decision, one I will make when I believe the conditions are right.

'I have read reports of financial demands and requests for full control that I have supposedly already made to the clubs mentioned, as well as reservations about what has been described as my "strong personality". These reports are unfounded, as there is currently no concrete basis for such assessments.

'Should a concrete opportunity arise, that will be the time to hold discussions with the club concerned and jointly consider the terms of a potential agreement, with due regard for both parties' needs and the qualities and approach that define my work as a manager.'

Pochettino, who landed the job at Old Trafford, has faced a whirlwind start having flown into Manchester following his final match in charge of the United States on Tuesday.

The Argentine took training for the first time on Thursday and will lead the Red Devils out for the first time on Sunday in a blockbuster clash with Liverpool at Anfield.

Pochettino takes over with Man United lying in the Premier League's relegation zone having won just one of their opening ten matches.

#1627. Liverpool confirm 22-man squad for Club Brugge as Cody Gakpo, Ryan Gravenberch decisions revealed

By Ben Knapton | 24 Nov 2026 13:08

Liverpool have confirmed their 22-man travelling squad for Wednesday's Champions League clash with Club Brugge at the Jan Breydel Stadion.

The Reds are going in search of their fourth win from five continental matches in Belgium, having overcome Atletico Madrid, Villarreal and LASK Linz before a 3-2 loss at Fenerbahce last time out.

Andoni Iraola's men have responded to that setback with back-to-back Premier League wins, though, following up a 3-1 triumph at Crystal Palace with a 4-0 battering of Manchester United on Sunday.

Teenage starlet Rio Ngumoha stole the show against the Red Devils in the absence of Cody Gakpo, who was an unexpected absentee from Sunday's matchday squad due to a calf injury.

Iraola revealed that Gakpo suffered his injury while on international duty with the Netherlands, and the attacker has not been included in the travelling party for Wednesday's game.

Gakpo's problem is not believed to be serious, though, and there is a chance that he will be fit to return for the weekend's Merseyside derby with Everton at the Hill Dickinson Stadium.

As well as Gakpo, compatriot Ryan Gravenberch will also miss Liverpool's trip to Brugge, as the midfielder continues his recuperation from a small heel fracture.

After the weekend's win over Man Utd, Iraola expressed hope that Gravenberch would be fit for the Champions League clash, having returned to training while carefully managing his pain.

However, the Netherlands international will now miss a fourth consecutive game for Liverpool, and he is still waiting for his first minutes of November, having also been an unused substitute against Arsenal.

Gravenberch and Gakpo are two of five Liverpool absentees against Club Brugge, as Hugo Ekitike (Achilles), Giovanni Leoni and Conor Bradley (both knee) have not made the cut either.

The rest of Liverpool's squad is as expected, and alongside Ngumoha, five other Kirkby youngsters could earn opportunities to impress at the Jan Breydel Stadion.

Nineteen-year-old midfielder Trey Nyoni could make his fourth consecutive start in the Champions League after appearing from the off against LASK, Villarreal and Fenerbahce, scoring against the latter.

Twenty-two-year-old James McConnell is also involved, but the midfielder has been restricted to just one nine-minute cameo in the UCL against Villarreal so far.

Wide man Luke Chambers, meanwhile, was given five minutes off the bench against LASK, but he has not made a single Premier League matchday squad this season.

Finally, attacking duo Lewis Koumas and Jayden Danns could earn valuable European minutes; the latter is yet to make a competitive appearance for Liverpool under Iraola.

Ferencvaros will be aiming to make it five wins in the league stage of the 2026-27 Europa League when they welcome Celje to Budapest on Thursday night.

The Greens will enter this match off the back of a 3-1 loss to Gyor in the league, while Celje recorded a 2-0 victory over Grosuplje in their last domestic game on November 22.

Ferencvaros have been excellent in this season's Europa League, beating Celtic, Viktoria Plzen, Torreense and AC Milan in the league stage of the tournament, with 12 points leaving them in third position in the table, level on points with the top two Benfica and Bournemouth.

Balazs Borbely's side were 2-0 winners over Milan in their last European match, which was a statement result, but their six-game winning run in all competitions came to an end on November 21 when they were overcome by Gyor in Hungary's top flight.

Ferencvaros reached the last-16 stage of the 2025-26 Europa League, ultimately losing to Braga, and they have been regulars in the knockout round of the competition of late.

It would be a shock if the Hungarian team were unable to progress to the knockout stage of this season's tournament given their strong position in the table.

Ferencvaros will take on Lech, Juventus and Hoffenheim in their final three games in the league stage of this season's Europa League.

Celje, meanwhile, have a record of one win, one draw and two defeats from their four matches in this season's competition, with four points leaving them down in 25th spot in the table.

The Yellow and Blues are opened their campaign with back-to-back losses to Bayer Leverkusen and Omonia before claiming a point in a 2-2 draw with Red Bull Salzburg.

Zoran Zeljkovic's side then recorded a 3-2 victory over Sturm Graz in their last European fixture, and Celje have actually won their last five matches in all competitions.

The Yellow and Blues have not been beaten since the 3-0 reverse to Omonia in the middle of October, so they will enter Thursday's match in strong form.

Celje played in the Conference League last season, reaching the last-16 stage of the tournament before going down 4-2 on aggregate to AEK Athens.

Ferencvaros will be missing Bence Otvos on Thursday through injury, while Bamidele Yusuf is suspended for the European fixture with Celje.

Kristoffer Zachariassen has been in excellent form this season, scoring 11 goals and registering nine assists in 25 appearances, and the 32-year-old will again be in the side.

Meanwhile, there should also be a spot through the middle for Lenny Joseph, who has six goals and three assists in 18 appearances during the current campaign.

As for Celje, no injuries have been reported ahead of the contest.

Svit Seslar has been the team's standout player this season from an attacking point of view, scoring 11 goals and registering two assists in 24 appearances, and the 24-year-old is set to start.

There is also expected to be a position through the middle for Armandas Kucys, who has netted five times for Celje during the 2026-27 campaign.

#1625. No advantage played and an indirect free-kick: Pairetto criticised for Milan-Frosinone officiating

Referee Luca Pairetto has been criticised for his performance in AC Milan’s 5-1 win over Frosinone last night.

This morning’s edition of La Gazzetta dello Sport (seen below) comments on three incidents above all in which the referee ultimately seemed incapable of providing the right decision, one of which could have cost a goal.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

In the first half, Adrien Rabiot stole the ball from Cittadini, who blatantly dragged him back by the shirt. The ball rolled to Goncalo Ramos who was through on goal and had a man to his left, effectively making it a two-on-zero break with just the goalkeeper to beat.

Yet, the referee Pairetto blew his whistle for a foul and showed a yellow card to the defender. He immediately apologised for his error in failing to play the clear advantage for the Rossoneri, in an incident reminiscent of the Junior Messias goal not given against Spezia in 2021-22.

That wasn’t all, either. Nine minutes into the second half, an indirect free-kick was awarded inside the Frosinone penalty area following a clear back-pass from Calvani to Palmisani, that was actually flagged by the assistant referee and not initially given by Pairetto.

Former referee Mauro Bergonzi commented on the refereeing incidents in Milan-Frosinone to La Domenica Sportiva.

“In the first half, the referee failed to take the lead: he missed the lead, he squandered it, if we’re being honest. The situation is this: Cittadini fouls Rabiot, who steals the ball, a clear hold, the referee hastily calls the foul, and he also realises it immediately because he stops, as if to say, ‘Wow, it’s a shame I called’ because Gonçalo Ramos was hurtling toward goal.

“He apologizes, he says: ‘No, I apologise, I’m booking the Frosinone player.’ He said sorry. But this is something that really bothers you from a refereeing perspective because the lead was clear, but the referee’s gesture is commendable because he raises his hands and humbly says: ‘I made a mistake’.

“53rd minute: we rarely see them called on football pitches during matches. It’s a deliberate back pass from Calvani to the goalkeeper, the goalkeeper saves it, the referee wouldn’t have called anything, he turns to the right, looks at the assistant because the assistant signals it to him.

“Pairetto tells the assistant, ‘Well done’ and, to make matters worse, ‘Well done’ again. The assistant was good because he saw it perfectly correctly. He made his choice, he got it right because this is a pass, a deliberate back pass.

“Chiffi, the fourth official, is also there, pressing the button to communicate with the refereeing team via his headset, and if the assistant hadn’t seen it, the fourth official would have signaled it.”

#1623. Harry Kane injury leaves Bayern Munich considering unlikely return

By Axel Clody | 24 Nov 2026 13:51

Just when his European career seemed to belong to the past, Eric Maxim Choupo-Moting could return to one of the biggest clubs in the world. Bayern Munich are studying a return for the Cameroonian forward to cover temporarily for the absence of Harry Kane.

Eric Maxim Choupo-Moting definitely has the art of appearing where no one expects him. At 37, after two seasons in Major League Soccer, the Cameroon international is among the solutions being considered by Bayern Munich to strengthen their attack this winter.

According to Sky Sport Germany, the former Paris Saint-Germain man's name was raised internally after Kane's injury. The Bavarian club do not have a genuine replacement centre-forward and are studying several options before the January transfer window. No final decision has been made yet, but the Cameroonian's candidacy exists.

A free agent at the end of his deal with New York Red Bulls, Choupo-Moting would be willing to sign for only six months, until the end of the season. He would also accept returning to the bench once Kane has recovered, without asking for any special status.

This profile has several advantages for Bayern Munich. The Cameroon international knows the club, its environment and the demands of the Bundesliga. He could be available immediately and would not need a long period of adaptation. Signing him would be a low-risk solution to accompany Kane's gradual return.

The mere fact that the Munich hierarchy are thinking of him says a lot about the esteem he left in Bavaria. Between 2020 and 2024, Choupo-Moting scored 38 goals in 122 appearances in all competitions. Initially signed to back up Robert Lewandowski, he managed to become a starter and to deliver when the Pole left the club.

After leaving for MLS following the end of his first spell at Bayern Munich, the Cameroonian made a successful start in New York. In 2025, he scored 17 goals and provided five assists in 33 regular-season games.

His playing time decreased in 2026, but he still scored five goals and provided one assist in only 538 minutes across 21 games. These figures show that his efficiency has not disappeared, despite a role that has become secondary.

This American stay could have been the quiet final stage of an already full career. Choupo-Moting could make the opposite journey and return to the Champions League, the Bundesliga and a dressing room he knows inside out.

Long reduced to a few famous misses during his time at Paris Saint-Germain, Choupo-Moting has built a career that few players can claim. Schalke 04, Stoke City, Paris, Bayern Munich and then New York: everywhere, he ended up getting playing time and making himself useful.

His honours include several French and German league titles, and he played in a Champions League final with Paris Saint-Germain. A return to Munich would be yet another snub to those who have often presented his presence at big clubs as an anomaly.

#1622. Ramos upset by substitution: The clarification and why Cisse came on over Camarda

Goncalo Ramos got his name on the scoresheet in AC Milan’s rout of Frosinone, but he was forced off in the second half.

As Sky (via Calciomercato.com) report, everything seemed great when Milan were dominating Frosinone at San Siro and scoring nearly every time they went forward. However, during the second half, a minor alarm sounded.

Ruben Amorim was forced to replace his Ramos in the 50th minute. The Portuguese striker – who had scored in the first half – was hastily removed from the pitch by the head coach shortly after Ardon Jashari’s goal to make it 3-1.

The reason? The change was made due to a minor muscle problem that the player reported to the bench, even though Ramos himself did not seem happy about the substitution at the time of the change.

The former PSG man informed the bench that he had a small calf problem and – to avoid worsening the issue – Amorim immediately opted for a substitution. Alphadjo Cisse was sent on in his place, and he scored the fourth goal just a few minutes later.

When he was taken off, Ramos showed a grimace of disapproval towards his bench, miming the ‘wait’ gesture. He then complained that he would have liked to try to stay on the pitch, but some post-match comments cleared things up.

When asked if his calf is ok, he told DAZN: “Yes, yes, everything’s fine, everything’s fine.” Rabiot later revealed the background to the substitution to Sky, admitting that he played a hand in convincing the coach.

“Gonçalo is the first player to do a lot. Today I saw he had a bit of pain in his thigh. I know he’s a very important player for us, and we have a lot of matches. I even asked the coach to let him rest a bit,” the Frenchman said.

Speaking to DAZN after the final whistle, Amorim was asked why he felt it was right for Cisse to come on rather than Francesco Camarda, the only other natural centre-forward in the squad

“We didn’t spend many minutes near the penalty area; he was behind. Today we were 40 metres from the goal, and Cisse was perfect for that. That’s why I didn’t bring on Camarda for Ramos: I needed someone who could run in behind.”
