When Wolverhampton Wanderers last attacked the Championship under a Portuguese manager new to English football, it proved a vintage season.

Molineux was under the spell of Nuno Espírito Santo in that 2017-18 campaign, and the big question is whether César Peixoto can lead a repeat nearly a decade later.

Peixoto was a surprise appointment in June, replacing Rob Edwards, and he has been entrusted with the mission of returning Wolves to the Premier League at the first time of asking.

“I have changed some things with set-pieces and some things in other moments of the game because I want the team to be organised and understand all the different moments within a match. During pre-season we have scored some goals from high pressing, but we will not be able to press high in every moment of every game. The players have to understand the game and recognise what each moment requires. It is important that we work as a team. When we can press high, we’ll press high. When we need to defend in a mid-block, we will stay organised. When the opposition pushes us deeper, which will sometimes happen, we have to be organised there as well.

“There are a lot of crosses in the Championship, for example, so the team needs to understand what to do in those situations. We want to play our football, be offensive and react strongly when we lose the ball, but we also need to understand the different moments of the game. I think we are at a good level to attack the Championship.”

Our experts have been having their say ahead of the new Championship season. A number of them believe Wolves will be promoted, including John Percy:

It is difficult to look beyond West Ham. Nuno Espírito Santo romped to the Championship title with Wolves in 2018 and remains a shrewd operator (along with his No 2 Rui Pedro Silva), while convincing Jarrod Bowen to stay is significant. I am going to go for Wolves and Middlesbrough as the other two promoted clubs.

The 2026/27 Championship season kicks off at Molineux as Wolves host Blackburn, with the home side hoping to put the bad memories of last season firmly behind them. There are new playoff rules in place for this season, with six places now up for grabs in the play-offs.

Wolves are aiming to return to the Premier League at the first attempt, having endured a miserable season in the top flight last year as they finished bottom with just three wins to their name. It has been a summer of change at the club as they chose to change managers. Rob Edwards lost his job in what was a shock move and was replaced by 46-year-old Cesar Peixoto, with this being his first head coaching position outside of his home country Portugal. Back in 2017/18, Wolves won the Championship title led by Peixoto’s compatriot Nuno Espirito Santo.

“I am ready,” Peixoto told Wolves’ club website. “We have worked very hard during pre-season, and I think we have had a great pre-season. All the players have worked very, very hard and they understand what I want from them. I am ready and confident going into the first game. Football is football, whether it is in Portugal or England, but there are different characteristics to the game here. We have watched, observed and analysed the Championship. We did that work before I came to the club, so we know what to expect.

“It is going to be a tough season with good teams, but we are prepared to fight for the three points game after game and week after week. We know what we want from the team and we know what our big goal is. We’re going to work very hard and fight to achieve that goal.”

They have brought in vast experience on the player side in the shape of Kieran Trippier and Raul Jimenez, who is back at Molineux three years after leaving for Fulham. Although they have lost Brazilian midfielder Joao Gomes to Aston Villa, most of their squad has stayed intact as they pursue promotion back to the top flight. It is a special year for the club as they celebrate their 150th anniversary.

Blackburn, led by experienced manager Tony Mowbray, did not enjoy a great season in the Championship last year, finishing down in 20th place and just five points above the relegation zone. 14 years have now passed since Blackburn last played in the top flight.

“I think it is a tough start,” Mowbray said. “On paper, I would suggest the first couple of games, particularly, jumped out as a tough start. One of the Premier League sides from last season, away from home. They have got a very talented squad, a pretty expensive squad. They have got some very good individual talent. Yet, there is an argument to say they have not won many football matches in the last calendar year. So, what we get, we will have to wait and see.”

These sides last met in the FA Cup during the 2024/25 season, with Wolves winning that fourth-round tie 2-0 thanks to goals from Matheus Cunha and Gomes, both of whom are now plying their trade elsewhere. The omens would appear to be on Wolves’ side as they are unbeaten in their last eight league meetings with Blackburn. Both sides progressed to the second round of the League Cup last weekend, with Wolves beating Port Vale 3-0 and Blackburn overcoming Burton Albion 2-1.

#1590. GdS: ‘Plays, scores and has fun’ – Pulisic the star in a Milan team rivalling the greats

Last night, AC Milan added another five goals to their tally in Serie A, making it one of their best starts to a season ever.

With Ruben Amorim, Milan are no longer the defence-first team that Massimiliano Allegri made them. Instead, they’re fluid, attacking and dangerous and the statistics show as much. So much so that their stars are shining brighter than they may have ever done before.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

As Gazzetta dello Sport writes, the Rossoneri are on fire, so much so that they’ve only outscored this season’s start twice in their history. With 28 goals in 12 games, everyone is helping things tick, but Pulisic, again, is standing out.

After a fine international break, the American ‘led the way’ again and added a goal to his tally for the season in fine fashion. He dons the superhero cape in a team that ‘plays, scores and has fun’ and with him, the team keep winning.

Every 87 minutes in the league, he’s contributed and for that reason, there’s a sense of inevitability seeing him in the teamsheet. Gazzetta writes that it’s effectively like entering every game with a 1-0 lead already.

He’s now scored in three consecutive games and it’s form that has not been bettered since the start of the 2024/25 season; where he scored four goals in a row. It’s not really a surprise, either.

In Ruben Amorim’s front-foot system, he’s one of the frontmen and that naturally means he’s going to score and create more. A ‘perfect match’ for Amorim, he’s leading in every sense and you’d have to look to the teams of Nereo Rocco and Lajos Czeizler for more goals – both teams scored 29 in their first 12 games of the Serie A season.

Ardon Jashari grabbing a goal also raised the number of scorers this season to eight, which is impressive in itself. It’s a ‘super-attacking’ team where everyone contributes, but Pulisic is again leading.

Amorim has taken the same players that Allegri had and completely changed their output and style. Amorim makes mistakes as he’s human but I don’t think we can honestly look at this team and say that. Amorim isn’t working out. He’s working out and given time and a few more transfer windows, I don’t see how we aren’t competing for UCL and Serie A for the next 5 years.

The team is actually quite different than last season. Gila Musah Cisse Ramos Diego makes 5 changes out of the 10 outfield players. Pulisic is also no longer being asked to play striker/ss and not surprisingly his form has returned. His manager is talking about how irreplaceable he is vs behind the scenes trying to have him sold.

Ah ya ok so 50% dif lol. Still, Rabiot and pulisic have hit absolute peaks under Amorim where as you said under allegri they struggled out of position. Rabiot recently said he doesn’t like playing deep and that’s where allegri had him. I’m surprised by Modric bc he wanted to sit back when he got here but he’s all over the place under Amorim. Also think Amorim is getting more out of players like Musah that previous coaches didn’t same with de winter and even salad maker before the injury. A lot of it is just trusting the players to use their talents and make the right choices on the pitch where as allegri had them all boxed in before the match even started.

An underrated reason for Pulisic’s emergence: Leao is gone.

Sure, Allegri’s style wasn’t a great match, and Puli had to play striker at times last year, which isn’t his best spot.

But when Leao was on the field in 2024 and 2025, he took all the focus, demanded the ball, demanded to be the center of attention. Now the team is much more balanced, with Morriera and Puli equally drawing the ball and Rabiot and Modric looking equally for them and for Ramos.

The real revelations for me this season are Moreira and Musah. We all knew what Rabiot and Pulisic are capable of under the correct system and football philosophy.

Jason Momoa Jr. – I knew nothing about him before he joined, but his raw power, speed, fighting spirit and confidence are well worth his big price tag. Pretty sure if he stays away from injuries, his form will only improve.

I’ve commented probably 100 times (before he went on loan) that Musah is very hard working, good bench player to fill holes in the squad, but ultimately is lacking football intelligence and cannot make more than 2-3 out of 10 correct choices when and how to pass. His execution was even more questionable. Before he went on loan, Conceicao substituted him twice after 20 or so minutes… With all this experience with our shirt, he came back and is one of the most reliable players on the field. Control, decision making, execution – it’s a completely different player.

#1589. Ajax vs Thun - prediction, team news, lineups

By Adepoju Marvellous | 24 Nov 2026 16:54, Last updated: 24 Nov 2026 20:35

Ajax and Thun face off at the Johan Cruyff Arena on Thursday as the 2026-27 Conference League campaign reaches its midway point.

Both teams emerged victorious in their last continental outings and now look to build on that momentum on the European stage.

Returning to action after agonisingly surrendering a two-goal lead to FC Twente before the international break, Ajax made light work of Eredivisie newcomers ADO Den Haag, cruising to a 3-0 victory on Sunday thanks to two goals from Davy Klaassen and a strike from Jorthy Mokio.

Michel’s side have now claimed six victories from their last seven matches in all competitions since losing to Hajduk Split in their Conference League opener in mid-October, with subsequent continental outings yielding wins over Atalanta and Midtjylland by a combined score of 8-1.

Central to De Godenzonen’s resurgence has been their ability to start quickly, with Klaassen's opener last time out marking the seventh consecutive match in which they have broken the deadlock.

Ajax currently sit outside the guaranteed knockout places in the Conference League and will be keen to collect maximum points to break into the top eight, thereby avoiding the additional hurdle of a playoff tie in an already congested campaign.

Thursday’s game marks the third meeting between the sides, with the hosts seeking to maintain their perfect record in this fixture, having come out on top in both group-stage encounters of the 2005-06 Champions League en route to a last-16 exit.

Thun ended a 13-year absence from European competition by qualifying for this season’s Conference League, but a pair of 1-0 defeats in their opening two matches against FC Twente and Hajduk Split meant their return to continental action began on a sour note.

Days after netting four times in the final 20 minutes of a nine-goal thriller against Lausanne-Sport to claim a remarkable triumph, Gian-Luca Privitelli starred against Scottish outfit Hearts, leading Thun to a 3-1 victory to finally get their European campaign up and running at the third attempt.

Back-to-back winless games against Basel and Young Boys have followed, so Die Oberlander head to Amsterdam with confidence low and knowing that a defeat could see them drop out of the knockout playoff places, so there is little margin for error.

Thun have conceded in each of their last 13 competitive matches, including 11 goals in their most recent four. Tightening up defensively will be essential if the Swiss side are to end their ongoing three-game losing run against Dutch opponents.

Thursday’s visitors have let in just one goal after half time across their three Conference League games so far, but against an Ajax side who have netted seven times in that period, they cannot afford any lapses in concentration over the course of the 90 minutes.

Attacking trio Simon Adingra, Kasper Dolberg, and Viktor Tsygankov are all ruled out through injury for Ajax, who welcomed back Anton Gaaei and Julian Brandt last time out.

Having only joined in mid-September, Yves Bissouma was not registered by the hosts for European competition, making him ineligible to feature on Thursday.

Tolu Arokodare has a tournament-high five direct goal contributions in the Conference League this term, and despite failing to find the net against ADO, he remains one to watch.

Genis Montolio and Fabio Saiz remain unavailable for Thun as they continue to recover from long-term knee injuries.

Furkan Dursun (leg) and Mattias Kait (back) both missed the visitors’ defeat to Young Boys, and neither is expected to return for Thursday.

Ter Stegen; Rosa, Kehrer, Janse, Wijndal; Klaassen, Baas; Gloukh, Mokio, Ouazane; Arokodare

Steffen; Mambwa, Bamert, Burki, Dahler; Maier, Zoukit, Roth, Reichmuth; Christoffersson, Labeau

Ajax are in imperious form and have won each of their last three home matches without conceding.

While the hosts may concede this time around, we fully expect them to claim victory and keep their momentum going.

#1587. Liverpool injury update: Andoni Iraola makes worrying Ryan Gravenberch admission - "Not in a good place"

By Ben Knapton | 24 Nov 2026 17:13, Last updated: 24 Nov 2026 17:13

Liverpool head coach Andoni Iraola has dropped a worrying admission over Ryan Gravenberch's fitness ahead of Wednesday's Champions League clash with Club Brugge.

The Dutchman has missed each of the Reds' last three games with a heel fracture and was unsurprisingly not included in Liverpool's 22-man squad for the trip to the Jan Breydel Stadion.

Gravenberch had returned to training before Liverpool's 4-0 win over Manchester United in Sunday's Premier League affair, but the former Ajax man is still no closer to a competitive comeback.

After landing in Belgium, Iraola fielded questions from the media in his pre-game press conference, and he admitted that Gravenberch's injury was proving more complex to solve than initially anticipated.

"With Ryan, it's a bit more difficult," Iraola said. "He's having pain, the things in the fascia are difficult to solve. Sometimes he's managing the pain, but now he's not in a good place. Let's see if we can find ways to solve the problem but they are injuries that are not easy to solve normally."

While the exact nature and severity of Gravenberch's injury is not entirely clear, the Netherlands international may be suffering from Plantar fasciitis, which would fit Iraola's description.

An inflammation of the heel, Plantar fasciitis can take anywhere between four and 12 weeks to get better, and Gravenberch has already been out since the beginning of November.

As a result, the Dutchman may be missing until the end of January in the worst-case scenario, meaning he would firstly miss matches against Chelsea, Tottenham Hotspur, Porto and Aston Villa before the end of the year.

Liverpool then face Manchester United, Inter Milan and Everton again in the early weeks of 2027, and it remains to be seen if Gravenberch's complex issue has settled down by then.

The 24-year-old has set up one goal in 12 appearances for Liverpool so far this season, and in his absence, Alexis Mac Allister, Trey Nyoni, Dominik Szoboszlai and James McConnell will be competing for midfield minutes.

As well as delivering a negative update on Gravenberch, Iraola also revealed that Cody Gakpo would likely miss the weekend's Merseyside derby with Everton too.

The attacker hurt his calf while representing the Netherlands during the international break, although Iraola has insisted that his issue is not severe.

"With Cody, it's a soleus injury," Iraola added. "It's not big but we expect he'll be out for the weekend. But it's more predictable."

Giovanni Leoni (knee), Conor Bradley (knee) and Hugo Ekitike (Achilles) are also on the sidelines for Liverpool, who sit eighth in the Champions League league-phase table with nine points from their opening four fixtures.

#1586. A footballer who loves getting cards! Tottenham star Tosin Adarabioyo opens up on his passion for collecting as he launches trading card shop in London with Chelsea's Reece James and Levi Colwill

Published: 18:00 EST, 20 November 2026 | Updated: 18:06 EST, 20 November 2026

Tottenham star Tosin Adarabioyo has joined forces with former Chelsea team-mates Reece James and Levi Colwill to launch a trading card shop in London.

Card Cop, opening in Borough Market on Thursday, will sell cards from a variety of sports as well as other collections such as Pokemon and Marvel.

Adarabioyo began collecting as a child and returned to the hobby in 2020. His collection, which he shares on social media, spans a variety of sports and he also has several of Brazilian icon Neymar.

'I’ve been collecting for years, and it’s great to see the hobby continue to grow,' said the 29-year-old, who left Chelsea for Spurs last summer.

'I love collecting. It’s a great way for supporters to connect with their favourite players. I’ve always felt that collectors are some of the most passionate fans.

'I’ve got to know so many collectors through the hobby. Talking about our collections is an instant icebreaker, and I know those conversations can mean a lot. I want to bring more players into the hobby and recreate those moments.

Tosin Adarabioyo, like many footballers, has a passion for collecting trading cards

The new shop is set to open in London's Borough Market next week

Adarabioyo enjoyes collecting cards of former PSG star Neymar, who won 130 caps for Brazil

'Neymar is criminally underrated to me, and I think his cards are too. Some of the images take me straight back to performances I’ve watched over the years. It’s hard to describe, but it’s like bottling up that feeling forever. Football purists will know what I mean.'

West Ham defender Kyle Walker-Peters, who played with Tosin at England youth level, is among backers along with James and Colwill.

Adarabioyo already has an online retail business, The Huddle, with guests such as Dominic Solanke, Robert Sanchez and Adam Wharton all featuring on live streams, opening boxes as fans watch.

Recent figures valued the global sports trading card market at $13.75billion (£10.5bn) in 2025, with that projected to grow to $27.52bn (£21bn) by 2034.

Formula One star Lewis Hamilton got in on the act earlier this year, launching his own venture and a shop in Frankfurt.

The seven-time world champion was already an ambassador for Topps - who also have the licence for Premier League cards - and said: 'I’ve loved collecting cards since I was a kid — Pokemon, football, anything I could get my hands on.

'To now play a role in shaping the future of the category is incredible. We have a significant opportunity to tap into the culture in a way no one has before.'

#1582. Opinion: Liverpool can solve two problems with incredible double transfer

Liverpool have many problems that they need to solve among their ranks.

Andoni Iraola's men are fourth in the Premier League table at the moment with seven points separating them and first-placed Arsenal.

Manchester City and Brighton are the two other teams ahead of them with one point between all three clubs.

Liverpool's rocky start to the season really didn't help matters much and is one of the main reasons why they are where they are right now.

However, with the January transfer window now just around the corner, Liverpool could take advantage of it and force their way back up the table.

Barcelona want to sell Gavi and Alejandro Balde in January

Two of the main positions that the Reds need to upgrade this winter are their left-back and centre-midfield.

Both positions have players among them that haven't met expectations at all this term.

This has led to a lot of underperformance from Liverpool and has forced them to continually experiment with the players that they have at their disposal.

In some cases, players such as Trey Nyoni and Lewis Koumas have massively benefitted from this but, in others, questions remain.

Many different players are on the Reds' shortlist but now, an update from journalist Juan Jesus may have just confirmed who the Reds' main targets could end up being.

"In addition to Alejandro Balde, Barça are now pushing Gavi out this very winter to fund the signing of a centre-back, seen as the club’s absolute priority," he wrote.

"The main target to bolster the defence is Nico Schlotterbeck, but the current wage bill leaves no room to pull off a move of that magnitude in January.

"To comply with financial fair play rules and try to sign him in this winter window, the board is pushing for two key sales: Balde on one hand, and the bombshell departure of Gavi on the other."

Gavi and Alejandro Balde would be two perfect signings for Liverpool

Most Liverpool fans will know that Balde has been linked with the Reds for a while now.

The Spaniard has been left out of Hansi Flick's plans this term with the La Liga giants making it clear since the summer window slammed shut that the 23-year-old had no future left at the Camp Nou.

His natural position is left-back but, he's also been used as a right-back in the past.

Gavi is a completely different kettle of fish altogether. The 22-year-old has played in 179 games throughout his career so far with his best position being a central midfielder.

During his time in Barcelona's first-team squad, he's helped Pedri boss many different midfields and has contributed to 28 goals across all competitions.

Right now, it's unclear how much either of them would cost but, since the Reds' relationship with Barcelona is strong, a deal could definitely be agreed.

Jack Grealish has been offered an olive branch by Everton boss David Moyes and said the sanctioned star is available for selection this weekend.

But Grealish will be considered for the squad when the in-form Toffees travel to Brentford on Monday night.

Jack Grealish is available for Everton again after serving his punishment and regaining fitness

#1577. Man United learn Leny Yoro appeal decision as the Football Association make their call

By Matt Law | 24 Nov 2026 18:47, Last updated: 24 Nov 2026 18:50

Manchester United will have Leny Yoro available for Saturday's Premier League clash against Brentford, with his one-game suspension being removed.

Yoro was sent off in the early stages of Sunday's Premier League clash with Liverpool following a last-man challenge on Reds forward Alexander Isak.

The France international was facing a one-game suspension, ruling him out of Man United's next Premier League fixture against Brentford.

However, the ban has now been removed following a successful appeal.

"Leny Yoro’s one-match suspension has been removed following a successful claim of wrongful dismissal," read a statement from the Football Association.

"The Manchester United player was sent off for denying an obvious goalscoring opportunity during their Premier League match against Liverpool on Sunday 22 November. The independent Regulatory Commission’s written reasons for its decision will be published in due course."

There had been a lot of debate surrounding whether the foul was a clear denial of a goalscoring opportunity, as Isak appeared to lose possession of the ball.

Breaking: Leny Yoro's red card against Liverpool has been overturned.? https://t.co/GIdwIWXdUs

Man United head coach Mauricio Pochettino and midfielder Kobbie Mainoo both criticised the decision in their post-match comments.

"The ball was for the goalkeeper. In that situation, if you review the VAR you can see for sure, [Yoro] never had the intention to connect with Isak," said Pochettino.

"When the control was long with the striker, the ball was going to the goalkeeper."

Mainoo, meanwhile, said: "The game's been taken out of our hands by a red card that I don't think can be a red card. No chance. The ball's already with the goalkeeper."

Yoro is currently with the Man United squad in Portugal preparing for Wednesday's Champions League fixture with Sporting Lisbon.

Enzo Maresca has made a total of five changes to his Manchester City starting lineup for tonight’s Champions League clash against Napoli at the Etihad Stadium.

Matheus Nunes has recovered from an ankle injury and is fit to start, while Enzo Fernandez, Rayan Cherki, Josko Gvardiol and Allan also come into the side following last weekend’s 1-1 Premier League draw with Fulham.

#1573. Chelsea slapped with huge £150,000 fine after 'f*** the Pope and the IRA' fan chants in last season's FA Cup tie at Charlton

Published: 11:24 EST, 20 November 2026 | Updated: 18:21 EST, 20 November 2026

Chelsea have been slapped with a significant £150,000 fine by the Football Association for their fans’ behaviour during an FA Cup away tie at Charlton Athletic more than ten months ago.

It was alleged that in the 56th minute, the visiting supporters at the Valley sang ‘f*** the Pope and the IRA’. A charge followed, and Chelsea were hit with their fine, along with being given an action plan to follow and a formal warning as to their future conduct.

Chelsea tried to appeal being fined £150,000 for the sectarian chanting. They wanted it either removed completely, or at least substantially reduced.

The club attempted to argue that it was excessive despite admitting that approximately 2,500 of their fans may have taken part in the offensive singing. They also noted how Millwall were previously not fined for the same chant occurring.

Their appeal was dismissed and the full scale of their punishment was upheld.

In a statement, Chelsea said of the chanting: ‘We unequivocally condemn this behaviour. Sectarian abuse – chanting that creates division targeted towards a particular religious or political group – and discriminatory language of any kind has no place in our football club.

Chelsea have been hit with a £150,000 fine for their fans’ behaviour during an FA Cup away tie at Charlton Athletic back in January

Xabi Alonso insists his Chelsea stars will show they are not 'soft' after Leeds United rubbed in how often they have bullied their opponents in a video uploaded to their social media.

Leeds produced a compilation of clips of their players leaving crunching challenges in on their Chelsea counterparts and capitalising on mistakes made down the years.

Daniel Farke's side have won more duels than any other club in the Premier League this season, and Alonso's team crumbled when visiting Sunderland before the international break. That was a game in which Levi Colwill and Co were bullied by Brian Brobbey. Colwill was hooked at half-time in that 1-0 loss at the Stadium of Light.

Dominic Calvert-Lewin may now be relishing testing Chelsea at Stamford Bridge, but Alonso said when asked about being seen as weak: 'We focus on not being soft and being competitive. That's our goal. We have played once this year (a 6-3 win for Chelsea in the Carabao Cup). We will play twice more (in the league). We are ready for that. I like that. We will show that.'

Calvert-Lewin shares similar attributes to Brobbey in that he is a traditional centre forward who will challenge Chelsea's centre backs.

'It¿s quite common in the Premier League that they have a good No 9,' Alonso said. 'Calvert-Lewin is doing well. He played with England. But it is up to us, how we defend, how we compete in those situations, how we attack the last line, how we attack their defenders. The preparation has, as always, we think been good. We are ready.'

Asked if defenders have forgotten how to face such strikers, Alonso added: 'Forgotten? No, no, no, I don't think forgotten. But it's demanding to play against No 9s. But I don't think it's been forgotten. But it's good they are back, these type of players.'

Only Tottenham have made more changes to their line-up than Chelsea this season, adding to the suggestion that Alonso is still searching for his preferred style of play. Some have been forced on the Spaniard because of their habit for picking up injuries despite playing only once a week.

'Once you have the whole menu, you can select what you like and I know what I like from the menu,' Alonso said. 'I would like to have more options with the whole squad available but that's something that's difficult to have during the season. I am sure we will get close to that.

'It (the injuries) is a concern. Sometimes you can analyse them and find a reason but sometimes it is difficult to find a reason.'

‘Such behaviour only serves to cause hurt to others and does not represent the values we hold as a club. We want to create a safe and inclusive environment for all, and we have a shared responsibility in delivering this.’

They added: ‘We understand that further incidents risk additional sanctions against the club and are doing everything we can to inform and educate supporters, as well as develop our existing initiatives to prevent, detect and respond to discrimination in future. We know Chelsea fans do not want to see any form of discrimination in our game, and we ask for their support in fostering a welcoming environment at Chelsea matches going forward.’

On the pitch, Chelsea will go into their Saturday clash against Leeds United without star striker Joao Pedro, who has yet to return to training.

Since the Brazilian was sidelined, Chelsea have won only one of their three Premier League games played, beating a beleaguered Manchester United under Michael Carrick. Otherwise, they have lost to Tottenham Hotspur and Sunderland without scoring.

Joao Pedro is still nursing a thigh problem, and has not yet made it outside with his team-mates as Leeds visit Stamford Bridge on Saturday. Chelsea will, however, have Moises Caicedo available after his injury scare during the international break with Ecuador.

‘He's not fit yet to train with the team, so we need to wait a bit longer,’ Alonso confirmed on Joao Pedro. He’s not going to be available for Leeds. We need to see game by game how he's feeling. So far we have tried different options and we need to keep trying.’

Chelsea will have Emiliano Martinez available after recovering from his broken jaw suffered at Everton on October 17. The goalkeeper required surgery following his collision with Jarrad Branthwaite. #1571. Sunderland vs Jagiellonia Bialystok - prediction, team news, lineups

By Oliver Thomas | 24 Nov 2026 19:00, Last updated: 24 Nov 2026 21:37

Sunderland resume their Europa League campaign on Thursday night with a matchday five fixture against Polish outfit Jagiellonia Bialystok at the Stadium of Light.

While the Black Cats currently occupy 11th place in the 36-team League Phase standings, Jaga find themselves down in 27th place at the halfway stage.

Sunderland’s first major European campaign in 53 years began with back-to-back victories over AZ Alkmaar (1-0) and Torreense (2-1), but they have since suffered setbacks against Lech Poznan and Dinamo Zagreb.

Regis Le Bris’s men were held to a 1-1 draw in Poland by Poznan on matchday three before, they were booed off by the Stadium of Light faithful following a disappointing 2-0 home defeat three weeks ago, seeing them slip out of the automatic last-16 qualification spots.

Since then, Sunderland supporters have had a lot more to be optimistic about, with four points collected and two clean sheets kept in Premier League matches against Chelsea and Aston Villa, beating the former at home 1-0 before drawing 0-0 away against the latter last weekend.

The Black Cats remain inside the Premier League relegation zone, but a renewed sense of resilience has given Le Bris’s side something to build on. Their defensive home form has been particularly pleasing, keeping four clean sheets in their last six home matches across all competitions.

With a tricky trip to Italian giants AC Milan looming on matchday six, Le Bris might view this encounter against Jagiellonia as a must-win opportunity if they wish to climb back into the top eight and ensure they avoid a playoff place.

Competing in the Europa League for the first time in their history this term, Jagiellonia have endured a difficult start to their League Phase campaign, losing three of their first four matches to leave them sitting one point outside of the knockout round playoff places.

The 2024-25 Conference League quarter-finalists responded to a 2-1 opening defeat to Olympiacos with a 3-1 home victory over Ararat-Armenia, but they have since been brought back down to earth by successive losses without scoring against Anderlecht (3-0) and Levski Sofia (1-0).

Thirty-four-year-old boss Adrian Siemieniec is now ready to fulfil one of his coaching “dreams” by taking his Jagiellonia side to a Premier League stadium, with Thursday’s fixture against Sunderland representing one of their toughest tests yet on the continent.

Seeking to avoid a third straight away loss in Europe will be even more challenging without any away supporters, as Jaga were handed a UEFA ban following crowd disturbances in their most recent loss to Levski Sofia.

On the domestic front, Siemieniec recently acknowledged that his team’s form has fallen far below expectations this term, with seven wins and seven defeats posted in 14 Ekstraklasa matches. A 3-1 defeat at KS Cracovia last weekend leaves them down in ninth place in the table, six points behind the top three.

Jagiellonia Bialystok Europa League form:

Jagiellonia Bialystok form (all competitions):

Sunderland will be without Granit Xhaka (calf), Brian Brobbey, Daniel Ballard, Habib Diarra (all thigh) and Romaine Mundle (knee) due to injury, while Jocelin Ta Bi, Melker Ellborg, Alan Browne and Aji Alese are all ineligible for the Europa League.

Although Trai Hume is one booking away from a European ban, he could continue on the right flank, unless Le Bris decides to recall either Malick Fofana or Nilson Angulo.

Enzo Le Fee has scored a team-high four goals this season – all penalties – and could operate in an advanced midfield role in front of Noah Sadiki and Jules Ahoka, while defensive trio Kevin Danso, Omar Alderete and Dayann Methalie will all be pushing to return after watching on as substitutes against Aston Villa.

As for Jagiellonia Bialystok, Ousmane Sow picked up a knock last weekend and has emerged as a doubt, but Norbert Wojtuszek recovered from injury to feature as an second-half substitute last time out and may be in a position to start at right-back ahead of Rodrigo Conceicao.

Jesus Imaz and Nik Prelec have scored seven goals each this term, but they are yet to make the net ripple in the Europa League this term. Nevertheless, the pair are strong contenders to start in centre-midfield and up front respectively.

Roefs; Meunier, Danso, Alderete, Methalie; Sadiki, Ahoka; Hume, Le Fee, Fofana; Isidor

Jagiellonia Bialystok possible starting lineup:

With Sunderland finding the net with just 4.8% of their shots in the League Phase thus far, and failing to score more than once in eight of nine outings at the Stadium of Light this season, their backline should continue to carry the heavy lifting due to persistent struggles in the final third.

Goals are unlikely to flow freely in another finely-balanced encounter on Wearside, but we are still backing Le Bris’s men to navigate their way to a slender victory on home soil.

#1570. Opinion: Liverpool need to compete for the next Virgil van Dijk

Liverpool have earned a reputation for recruiting some of the best young players in world football in recent seasons.

The additions of Rio Ngumoha, Trey Nyoni and more recently Jeremy Jacquet and Luca Brughmans are proof of the philosophy in place within Liverpool's recruitment team.

With Julian Ward at the helm, the recruitment strategy doesn't seem to have changed, and the Reds continue to be linked with some of the most promising young talents from across Europe and beyond.

Liverpool's mission remains the same but that doesn't mean that they are automatically the favourites for every wonderkid, and they appear to be falling behind in the race for one highly rated defender.

Liverpool behind in race for next Van DijkRuud Nijstad is quickly becoming one of the most exciting prospects in the Eredivisie, and the Dutch U19 international is earning himself plenty of attention. The 18-year-old has started all but one game for FC Twente in the league this season, and has established himself as a central part of John van den Brom's side. Standing at 6'5, Nijstad already holds the stature of a Premier League defender, and his impressive performances for Twente, both domestically and in the UEFA Conference League, have led to interest from several top sides.

Ruud Nijstad is quickly becoming one of the most exciting prospects in the Eredivisie, and the Dutch U19 international is earning himself plenty of attention.

The 18-year-old has started all but one game for FC Twente in the league this season, and has established himself as a central part of John van den Brom's side.

Standing at 6'5, Nijstad already holds the stature of a Premier League defender, and his impressive performances for Twente, both domestically and in the UEFA Conference League, have led to interest from several top sides.

Having the chance to learn from the man who captain's his national team could be vital for Nijstad, who could command a fee of over €30 million (~£25m) according to Konur.

Liverpool clearly aren't leading the race for Nijstad, but he would be an excellent January pick up and Ward & Co should definitely be taking a look at the 18-year-old.

#1569. Newcastle kit fiasco sums up haphazard pre-season

Newcastle’s pre-season friendly against Bayer Leverkusen at St James’ Park took a bizarre turn when a kit clash prompted the hosts to change shirts midway through the first half.

The German team’s white away kit with blue trim proved hard to distinguish from Newcastle’s home strip, which has a white back and blue stripes across the shoulders.

During the first-half hydration break, Newcastle decided to change into their lilac third kit, which improved the viewing experience for fans who took to social media to question the original choice of kits.

Newcastle would go on to lose the game 2-1 in new manager Matthias Jaissle’s first game at St James’, a result which followed a 3-1 reverse against Everton on Wednesday evening.

Leverkusen, the 2023-24 Bundesliga champions now managed by Spaniard Carles Martínez Novell, scored after just 44 seconds through a powerful Ibrahim Maza strike.

Jaissle’s team found their feet as the first 45 minutes progressed, with Yoane Wissa their biggest attacking threat. The striker endured a difficult first season at the club, but his performances at the World Cup with DR Congo appear to have restored confidence.

Newcastle were level just before half-time, when Malick Thiaw rose highest to plant home a back-post header from a corner. Former Brentford goalkeeper Mark Flekken appealed in vain for a foul, but there was no infringement.

After changing all 10 outfield players at half-time against Everton, Jaissle was more circumspect with second-half substitutes; Rory Finneran for Lewis Miley was the only change before the 80th minute.

Newcastle faded though, and the game was won by Victor Boniface scoring just a few minutes after coming on as a substitute. The Nigeria striker wrong-footed Sean Steur with an impudent piece of skill before rolling the ball into the bottom corner.

The North-East club are coming to terms with the departures of Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and Bruno Guimarães this summer, as well as manager Eddie Howe. They have one more pre-season friendly to play, against Strasbourg on Sunday, before they begin their Premier League campaign at home to Liverpool.

Newcastle United (4-2-3-1) Hornicek; M Miley (Pivas 81), Thiaw, Botman, Hall; Steur, L Miley (Finneran h-t); Elanga, Woltemade (Neave 86), Barnes; Wissa. Subs Charlton, Harris (g), Sanusi, Johnson.

Bayer Leverkusen (4-2-3-1) Flekken; Vazquez (Tape h-t), Bade, Tapsoba, Gutierrez (Belocian 70); Garcia, Fernandez (Terrier 70); Maza (Boniface 80), Tillman (Doganay 70), Moreira (Tella 80); Kofane (Schick h-t). Subs Hofmann, Arthur, Oermann, Poku, Blaswich (g), Alfa-Ruprecht, Hawighorst, Lomb (g).

Referee Michael Oliver (Durham). Attendance 39,059

A second pre-season defeat in a week for Newcastle. Just like against Everton, they faded in the second 45 minutes but Jaissle decided to leave some tired legs out there for fitness purposes. The performances of Barnes and Wissa were promising, but Newcaslte are giving up chances.

Newcastle had a free-kick with the last kick of the game, but Harvey Barnes loops the delivery straight into Flekken’s gloves.

Schik with a chance to wrap up the victory, but Hornicek saves before Thiaw clears to deny Terrier a tap in on the rebounds.

There will be just three minutes of added time to play.

Elanga fouled near the touchline, but time is running out. The free-kick won by Neave came to nothing.

Chance for Barnes! Good combination play involving Elanga and Wissa down the right, and the ball flashed across the six-yard box. Barnes almost steered it in, but did not make firm enough contact.

Newcastle attacking with more urgency since conceding, but there are moans and groans in the ground at a misplaced Elanga pass. Sean Neave has just replaced Woltemade, and the 19-year-old wins a free-kick in a crossing position with his first action of the game.

The striker has only been on the pitch a few minutes, but Boniface has restored Leverkusen’s lead. Lovely chop inside the box, which sent Steur for a hot dog, before passing the ball into the far corner. No celebration of note from a player who could be on the move this summer.

Newcastle making just their second change of the game: Pivas replaces Mason Miley at right-back.

Leverkusen have made two more changes: Moreira and Maza off, Tella and Boniface on.

The corner is straight down the throat of Flekken, and that prompsts some groans from the home fans.

Newcastle having to defend deep for long periods, but Elanga did well to win a free-kick with little support. Moreira dragged the winger down. Then Wissa’s cross is turned behind for a corner.

Woltemade’s control lets him down as he tries to bring the ball down on halfway. The game is being played at a snail’s pace at the moment, but Leverkusen are dominating the ball.

Play has now resumed. Garcia does well to defend after Lewis Hall won the ball back in a dangerous position.

Time for another hydration break and Leverkusen are making three more substitutions. We await further changes from Jaissle. Should the game finish level, there will be a penalty shoot-out to decide the winner of the Visit Malta Cup.

Rather like the mid-week friendly against Everton, Newcastle have faded after half-time. Struggling to get into the game in any meaningful way. Slick football from Leverkusen but Fernandez fails to bring the ball under his spell in the box when there was time and space to shoot.

Leverkusen just inches away from regaining the lead. It was an incisive run off the left from Afonso Moreira, who tried to place the ball into the far corner but his attempt rolled just wide of the post.

Good defensive header by Lewis Hall before Wissa wins a foul on halfway. Newcastle feeding off scraps at the moment. Elanga goes too early and is flagged offside.

Bayer Leverkusen have had the better of it in this half, but some of the shooting has been wayward. This time is it Schik’s turn to slash a shot over the bar. Fouls committed by Finneran and Botman.

Newcastle with a three-on-three on the break after Wissa does well to win the ball back on halfway, but Woltemade was too slow to get his shot away at the end of the move. More good play from Wissa.

Half a chance for Fernandez to shoot from the edge of the D, but he was leaning back and ballooned the shot miles over the bar.

Finneran, the youngster in Newcastle’s midfield, is caught on the ball but then does well to recover it. I reckon there will be a raft of changes on the hour mark.

Corner for Leverkusen after Moreira gets forward and attacks Mason Miley. The German side have additional aerial threat with Schik on the pitch. Woltemade does well to head clear.

Bayer Leverkuen kick off in the second half.

Jaissle made 10 against Everton, so wants his starters to build minutes today. Rory Finneran is coming on for Newcastle, an 18-year-old academy player. He replaces Lewis Miley in midfield. Czech striker Patrik Schik is on for Bayer Leverkusen.

The scoreline is a fair reflection of an even first half, with Wissa Newcastle’s best player. The story though, is that kit clash that prompted Newcastle to change into their lilac third kit halfway through the half.

Just the two minutes of stoppage time to play.

Newcastle equalise from a set-piece. Flekken is claiming a foul, but it is a legitimate goal. The goalkeeper was nowhere to be seen on a corner that looped all the way to be back post, and he seemed to lose his bearings allowing Thiaw to find the far corner.

Newcastle have a corner after another move in which Wissa was lively. His performances have been a ray of light in pre-season, he really struggled in his first season at the club.

Lewis Hall takes the free-kick, but he scoops it well over the bar. Elanga delivers a low cross from the right, but Garcia is well positioned to clear.

Newcastle enjoying a lot more possession now, but you cannot say they look like equalising.

That was better though, more zip in the attack with Elanga laying the ball off for Wissa and Fernandez is booked from dragging the Newcastle forward to the ground. Free-kick in a shooting position.

Good play from Lewis Hall, skipping beyond two challenges to escape from a tight spot but then his crossfield pass is intercepted. Moreira passes the ball straight out of play for a Newcastle goal kick, when there was a chance for Leverkusen to punish the hosts on the break.

Elanga tries to take on Gutierrez but his low cross is too close to Flekken. Gutierrez then buys a foul when under pressure from Lewis Miley. Game has become quite bitty following those stoppages. Maza then chops down Harvery Barnes.

The game is back under way. Changing kits has improved things visually but it is still not ideal. You wonder how on earth two clubs of this stature failed to liaise on this before the game.

Bayer Leverkusen are still on top, but play has been stopped for a hydration break. Some boos from the stands, it is not an especially hot day.

On the subject of the kit clash, Newcastle are now changing into their lilac away kit. Shades of Manchester United at the Dell all those years ago.

A short stoppage in play after Tapsoba receives a knock in the small of the back from Newcastle’s goalkeeper Hornicek. Both managers get their players over for a tactical conflab.

Leverkusen look very accomplished in possession, they are moving the ball well through the lines. Kofane was a big threat when they played Arsenal in last season’s Champions League and they are looking to find him with crosses. Mason Miley defends well at right-back, but at the expense of a corner.

Flekken called into action again, Newcastle starting to warm to their task. It was direct play from first Elanga and then Barnes, but his cross deflects towards the goalkeeper and he parries away. Then Barnes is fouled, and Newcastle have a free-kick in a crossing position near the left corner of the penalty area. Poor delivery from Barnes, Flekken claims.

Newcastle fans sing “walking in a Keegan wonderland” in unison. Bade is then penalised for catching Woltemade late as they contested an aerial challenge.

Newcastle’s best moment so far: Wissa peels off the shoulder of Bade and tested Flekken with a volley from a tight angle. The goalkeeper saved and Leverkusen scramble clear, but it was good movement from the Newcastle striker.

Leverkusen continue to make the running, enjoying more possession and most of it is coming inside Newcastle’s half. Goalkeeper Flekken takes a beat inside his own six-yard box, and his pass out is almost cut out by Woltemade.

Newcastle’s players are wearing black armbands in memory of Kevin Keegan.

There is a slightly awkward clash of kits on display: both shirts feature a lot of white, and the blue trim around the shoulders of Newcastle’s home kit is quite similar to Leverkusen’s away strip.

Kofane, who impressed up front last season in Germany, throws himself at a cross.

Fans were barely settled in their seats when Maza’s vicious left-footed strike from outside of the area flew past Hornicek. Cracking goal, not much the goalkeeper could do about it.

Matthias Jaissle walks to the home dugout for the first time as manager. Just eight days until the proper stuff begins against Liverpool, a fixture which tends to throw up entertaining games. Bayer Leverkusen keep the home players waiting in the tunnel.

The former Liverpool defender has been linked with a move to Arsenal this week. Quansah is with his team-mates but not part of the matchday squad.

Bayer Leverkusen XI: Flekken; Gutierrez, Bade, Fernandez, Moreira, Tillman, Tapsoba, Arthur, Garcia, Maza, Kofane

Subs: Blaswich, Lomb, Hofmann, Terrier, Schick, Oermann, Tape, Poku, Vazquez, Boniface, Tella, Alfa-Ruprecht, Doganay, Hawighorst

Newcastle XI: Hornicek; M Miley, Thiaw (c), Botman, Hall; Steur, L Miley; Elanga, Woltemade, Barnes; Wissa

Subs: Harris, Charlton, Pivas, Sanusi, Johnson, Finneran, Neave

Today's team to take on Bayer Leverkusen in the @VisitMalta Weekender 👊 pic.twitter.com/ZfRvucBXSq

Newcastle United continue their preparations for the new season with a home friendly against Bayer Leverkusen, hoping to improve on their pretty limp showing against Everton at Murrayfield.

New manager ​Matthias Jaissle is ‌refusing to dwell on the departure of key players that has left his club in turmoil going into the Premier League season, insisting that he sees opportunity in the situation. Jaissle was recruited from Saudi Pro League side Al-Ahli after Eddie Howe left last month, with the German coach joining a club who had lost Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and captain Bruno Guimaraes in quick succession.

“It’s a challenge, a big challenge, always when there’s a transitional period. ‌But it’s ‌not time to ⁠complain, it doesn’t make sense to see the negative things,” Jaissle said.

“We want to see the chance in that situation and that’s our approach from day one. We are here to do our ⁠best job. We want to support the players, the current squad.

“There will be adjustments to see in the coming days, weeks. But for now it’s only focused on the daily work, the work we can influence. That’s all that ​matters now.”

The 38-year-old coach arrived in Newcastle ‌having won two Austrian Bundesliga titles with Red Bull Salzburg before leading Al-Ahli to back-to-back AFC Champions League crowns.

He remained tight-lipped about new signings.

“Obviously, in that transition phase, the players who left the club were ‌great ​players, great characters, experienced ⁠players. This is now a vacuum,” he said.

“Either we adjust something in the squad, by signing these players, these profiles, or other players ⁠need to step up and fill ​these positions, these leadership roles. I’m quite optimistic, we can work in both scenarios.”

Jaissle said he had a ​clear vision of how he wants his team to play.

“The phrase how Newcastle ‌should play like is front-footed, intense, ​aggressive and of course also successful. ​In the end, it’s all about what ⁠I can ⁠say and it’s also why I’m sitting here,” he said.

“The approach we have as a coaching team and the identity of Newcastle is famed for, it’s so linked so close together - which is a perfect fit in my eyes and ​that’s going to be exciting.”

#1568. Doubts over Olise and Musiala as Bayern target three rising Premier League stars

By Alexis Pereira | 24 Nov 2026 19:18

Bayern Munich have doubts over the long-term futures of Michael Olise and Jamal Musiala and are reportedly considering three Premier League wingers. After securing Harry Kane’s extension until June 2029, the Munich hierarchy now have two more delicate cases to handle.

The first is Olise, who has attracted interest from Real Madrid and Barcelona. Arsenal have just joined the list of suitors, while Liverpool and Manchester City are also following his situation. Bayern want to extend the French star’s contract, which currently runs until 2029, but no agreement has yet been found.

The Bavarian club also have doubts over Musiala’s long-term future. According to TeamTalk, several Bayern officials are said to question his ability to regain his best level, as the German attacking midfielder suffers absences linked to a ‘neurological dysfunction’.

The British outlet reveals that Bayern are following three Premier League players closely. The first is Liverpool’s young prospect Rio Ngumoha. The 18-year-old winger’s profile appeals to the German hierarchy, but Liverpool are reportedly close to signing him to a new long-term deal, which would seriously complicate Bayern’s ambitions.

The Munich club are also said to be keeping an eye on Florian Wirtz. Already highly rated in Germany after his rise at Bayer Leverkusen, the 23-year-old Germany international remains a prime target, though his importance to Liverpool makes a transfer hard to bring about.

Vincent Kompany is also said to have noted the name of his compatriot Jeremy Doku. The Belgian manager knows the Manchester City winger well, but there is a snag: the 24-year-old extended his contract with City until June 2031 this summer.

Bayern therefore appear to be at a disadvantage in signing any of these three rising Premier League stars, unless there is a dramatic turnaround. At the same time, the German side are also reportedly studying Bundesliga solutions, following Ibrahim Maza, Said El Mala and Antonio Nusa.

#1567. AC Milan 5-1 Frosinone: Five things we learned – centrality and consistency

AC Milan put on a show at San Siro on Sunday night as they swept Frosinone aside emphatically, beating them 5-1.

The own-goal that Gabriele Calvani scored a few minutes in set the tone for the visitors, while Goncalo Ramos broke his drought after starting and finishing a counter-attack. However, Patrizio Masini’s goal shortly after meant the deficit was halved going into the break.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

In the second half, Milan ran riot. Ardon Jashari and Alphadjo Cisse both had opportunities after being found in behind, and both just minutes after coming off the bench. Then, Christian Pulisic added the finishing touch to make it a five-star night.

It was a win that Milan needed, considering that only Inter out of the current top six, dropped points, and it moves the Rossoneri back into the top four spots. Ivan Stoev has picked out the key talking points from the game.

Technically, Rabiot won the MOTM in our post-game ratings, but we absolutely have to talk about Luka Modric.

I’ve personally had my doubts about the Croatian being able to keep up this season, especially under Ruben Amorim. We all expected the Portuguese coach to bring a lot of intensity to Milan’s game and at times, Modric has seemed to struggle.

Maybe that was because of the team adapting to the new coach, or maybe the midfielder hadn’t completely recovered after the World Cup – who knows.

The reality is that the former Real Madrid man has stepped up after some shaky games at the start of the season and continues to prove his quality on and off the ball and his athleticism and longevity are nothing short of extraordinary.

The vision and passing ability to play the through ball to Rabiot for the opening goal was world-class. He then continued to dictate the tempo and make impressive forward runs, playing the full 90 minutes, giving it his all until the final whistle.

The management really needs to assemble a whole group of people tasked to find a proper replacement for Modric, as he will leave a big gap in that midfield.

To continue with the midfielder theme, we also have to give praise to Rabiot, who has been absolutely brilliant this season. Don’t get me wrong, he was one of the Rossoneri’s best players last year too.

Yet he has found a higher level since the start of the campaign, as he racked up another two assists and forced the own goal. As a result, he now has five goals and seven assists in 10 games in Serie A – extraordinary numbers.

On top of the goal contributions, you can count on the Frenchman to be composed under pressure, tidy with his passing, and efficient in both phases of the game. An absolutely stunning start of the season for Rabiot, who is finding new levels to his game under Amorim.

It was such a dominant win that we can probably cover each player and the positives from their game. Nevertheless, one man needs to be praised for sure and that’s Goncalo Ramos, who got himself back on the scoresheet.

Needless to say, he opened up a lot of spaces for his teammates and had a role in some of the other goals, which he was doing even when he failed to get the ball in the back of the net. This time around, he also got his long-awaited goal.

It was a beauty too, in the sense that he dropped deep into his own half, made the tackle to win the ball and kicked off the counter-attack. Following that, he made the run into the opponent’s box and finished it calmly – it was beautifully orchestrated with Ramos in the centre.

The goal and the encouraging performance are also a relief, as we’ve seen many times how strikers struggle to react when they are not scoring, with the confidence level often dropping which results in overall poor form.

However, the Portuguese striker is clearly not in his head and reacted well to a poor spell that spanned both his club and the national team, as he struggled in the international break too.

We didn’t even see that much of him as Amorim subbed him off rather early and it probably has to do with the fact that Milan need a win on Thursday against Olympiacos, in Greece, and Ramos will most likely start the game as the margin for error is little as things stand.

I mean, what more can you ask from your attackers? Diego Moreira got the hockey assist on the second goal and got an assist for Cisse in the second half and on top of that, was heavily involved and dangerous when the Diavolo went on the counter.

Truthfully, the Belgian should have probably scored a goal or two as he had some very good chances in the opponent’s penalty box, but his shooting let him down this time around. Nevertheless, another electric performance.

Speaking of electric – Pulisic also did very well as he was involved in the first goal – even if it ended up being an own goal, his run forced the Frosinone defender to run back and eventually put the ball in his own net.

The American then got his goal in the second half with a composed finish. He had a very solid game overall with lots of smart movements and combination play- nothing flashy, but the efficiency was there.

Then we also have Cisse, who started the game on the bench but only needed nine or so minutes after coming on to get his goal. Ridiculously, he now has six in 10 in the league or a goal every 74 minutes. The youngster made a good run and managed to keep himself onside in a tricky situation and then finished with composure.

The variety in attack by Milan on the night was a joy to watch, as all the players posed a threat to Frosinone, which in the end was too much for them to handle.

Amorim was well aware of how Frosinone would approach the game, which in itself deserves credit as they came to San Siro to play football instead of sitting back. Unfortunately for them and fortunately for us, the coach and his players knew exactly how to get around the high press.

The Rossoneri were rapid on the counter and created so many chances that the score could’ve easily been even worse for Frosinone. Their high press also didn’t work, as for the majority of the game the Diavolo managed to move the ball around quickly enough, which prevented their opponents from winning it in dangerous areas.

It also must be said that the Portuguese did well to rest some key players after the third goal, as he will need a fresh lineup for the Europa League fixture on Thursday, where Milan need three points against Olympiacos.

Welcome to our Live Comments section, where new comments will appear automatically

Also, it was Pulisics’ pass to Moreira that set-up Cisse’s goal. If were recognizing “hockey assists” then Pulisic’s pass to Moreira was also world-class. Not to be a wet-blanket, but Moreira and Cisse need to develop composure on the ball. Too often Moreira would negate his speed on the ball by dribbling into multiple defenders without looking to pass to an open teammate. Against the top teams Milan will not have as many goal scoring opportunities as they did on Sunday so now is the time to work on finding the open man in the final third.

So young players with potential, need to learn to be better and realise thier potential.

It was a pass in a 3v3 counter-attack situation. Great pass but Modric took out 5 defenders with 1 move. That is why it is world class and Pulisic pass is not mentioned as much.

Did anyone notice how Pulisic slowed down his run, thus letting Ramos reach the penalty box earlier and score his long awaited goal? Such a team player..

He’s always been that guy. Sometimes I wish he can be more ‘selfish’. Another example is the penalty fiasco with Tammy back then.

Yet some people here have called him selfish many times – especially last season when he wasn’t scoring. But then again, those same people praised Leao and probably thought he was Ballon d’Or material. LOL. 🤦‍♂️😂😂😂

Yes. I’d say it was as much about letting Ramos score as it was about “arriving” in the box late, setting up a cut back score, which he learned from Frank Lampard. Both are good things.

#1566. I've been to all 92 grounds in the Premier League and Football League and this is my definitive ranking from worst to best - where does YOUR club end up?

Published: 21:00 EST, 20 November 2026 | Updated: 21:00 EST, 20 November 2026

Some grounds are beautiful. Some grounds are not so beautiful. Some grounds take you to the heart of the English game. And some leave you feeling like you're on the periphery.

But each of them holds the soul of their community and the hopes and dreams of the thousands of people who make the pilgrimage there every weekend.

On April 1, 2025, I made the trip to Harrogate Town’s Exercise Stadium and first fulfilled the quest of a lifetime by completing the set of all 92 English Football League grounds for Daily Mail Sport. But then Everton moved away from Goodison Park and into a stunning new stadium on the banks of the River Mersey.

I was one short again but on February 23, 2026, I got back up to 92 by going to Hill Dickinson Stadium to watch Everton versus Manchester United. Then, in November, with York City being promoted (alongside Rochdale, whose ground I had ticked off decades ago), I made the trip to the LNER Stadium to make the 92 whole again.

I won’t give too much away just yet, but why are grounds like AFC Wimbledon and Exeter City in my top 20? What about Anfield, Old Trafford and Stamford Bridge? Where does Everton’s dazzling new home rank? Where is the best grub in the Premier League and where did Tyson Fury once threaten to have my jaw broken?

This is my love letter to English football. Read on to find out who comes out on top, where your team ranks and everything else in between – then let me know what you think of my guide to the 92 grounds of England.

Division: Championship Opened: 1993 Capacity: 19,369

Being banned from The Den is the football equivalent of being banned from your local abattoir

I’ve been banned from The Den for the last 20 months, in a professional capacity anyway. I could still go in a personal capacity but, on balance, I think I’d rather not.

The Daily Mail has been told that our reporters are not welcome at the club because we had the temerity to report on the horrendous challenge by Millwall goalkeeper Liam Roberts on Crystal Palace’s Jean-Philippe Mateta during the FA Cup tie at Selhurst Park in March last year, which left the French striker requiring 25 stitches in his left ear.

Let’s be honest about this: there are worse places to be banned from. Being banned from The Den is the football equivalent of being banned from your local abattoir. You don’t have to be a racist, misogynistic, homophobic bloke with anger issues and a penchant for tragedy-chanting to feel at home at The Den. But it helps.

And, yes, I know Millwall are trying to rebrand themselves as a ‘family club’ now and the odd Tarquin and Tabitha stray across the county lines from Blackheath and Clapham to keep it real but that just makes The Den experience even worse.

The last time I went as a supporter was 16 years ago to watch Stockport County play there and the walk from South Bermondsey station to the away turnstiles was an eye-opener.

Not that there were any problems: even at Millwall, football has moved on since the 70s. But this still felt deeply dystopian: for their own safety, away fans walk to the ground through a long wire mesh cage that seems to have no end. It felt like embarking on a tour of Jurassic Park: you know that if the fences fail, the dinosaurs are going to take a run at you.

Inside the ground, which is modern and neat and relatively characterless, the level of hatred for visiting supporters feels unusually visceral. It’s loud. I’ll give it that. It’s primeval. It’s unreconstructed, which can be a good thing, too, and it breeds a sense of togetherness.

If medievalism is your thing, you’re in for a treat. If not, give it a miss.

Division: League One Opened: 2007 Capacity: 30,303

I know it’s a soft target but I really don’t care much for Stadium MK. Or for MK Dons, for that matter

I know it’s a soft target but I really don’t care much for Stadium MK. Or for MK Dons themselves for that matter.

The club was born under a bad sign when it was jemmied out of Wimbledon and moved to Milton Keynes in 2003 and it has never been able to shake the stigma since. The stadium fits the club.

It is a soulless, faceless, gloomy place. More than that, there is something rather forbidding about it. Its 30,000 capacity is too big for the club it hosts and, apart from the joys of the local KFC and McDonald’s, there is little to recommend in its immediate surrounds. Its black seats lend it a sinister air, too.

It’s the kind of stadium only its mother could love. And it doesn’t have a mother. Unless you want to do the 92, give it a miss.

Division: League One Opened: 2001 Capacity: 12,537

The empty end kills a lot of the atmosphere, although the Oxford fans are to be commended for the noise they do generate

I feel ashamed to say it, given that it is my local club, but the best experience I’ve had at the Kassam Stadium was getting my Covid jab there during the pandemic.

When they moved, around the turn of the century, abandoning the chaotic charm of the Manor Ground in Headington and swapping it for an isolated plateau outside the city, they only completed three sides, abandoning the fourth because of rising costs.

A particularly bitter wind blows in off the car park behind one of the goals and, from the main stand – in fact, from every stand – there is a magnificent and uninterrupted view of the Frankie and Benny's in the mini retail park that abuts the ground.

The empty end kills a lot of the atmosphere, too, although the Oxford fans are to be commended for the noise they do generate given they have endured a generation of being stuck here. Firoz Kassam still owns the stadium but not the club. That kind of separation always spells trouble.

Oxford are hoping to move to a new stadium to the north of the city in a couple of years’ time. It can’t come soon enough.

Division: Championship Opened: 2012 Capacity: 62,500

It was a great athletics arena and home to a whole host of golden memories at London 2012 but it’s a dog’s dinner of a football ground

I don’t even like calling it the London Stadium. It’s the Olympic Stadium, but it suited the David Sullivan-Karren Brady rebrand of the club to give it the capital’s name.

It was a great athletics arena and home to a whole host of golden memories at London 2012 but it’s a dog’s dinner of a football ground. It’s also a monument to much that is wrong with the upper reaches of the English game: a surrender of identity and tradition as collateral damage in the owners’ pursuit of profit.

Walking to it, sadly, feels a bit like walking through a wasteland and its odd configuration inside harms the atmosphere even though the fans are right up there with the best in the country. The old stadium at Upton Park was intimate and raucous and intimidating. The London Stadium is nothing like that.

The owners spent a lot of time congratulating themselves on the deal they did to move to the new ground: they’re the archetypes of football owners who know the price of everything and the value of nothing.

Division: League One Opened: 1899 Capacity: 34,835

It is hard to get past Hillsborough's association with so much death and despair and heartbreak and the betrayal of supporters

I used to think of Hillsborough as one of the cathedrals of the English game but since the disaster that claimed the lives of 97 Liverpool fans in 1989, it is hard to get past its association with so much death and despair and heartbreak and betrayal of supporters.

I know, obviously, that this would punish Wednesday fans who do not deserve to be punished for something that had nothing to do with them but Hillsborough, and its Leppings Lane End in particular, has such a cursed legacy that part of me thinks it should have been demolished and that the club should have moved elsewhere.

Even in the last couple of years, fans of Newcastle United and Leeds United have reported serious safety concerns in the Leppings Lane End.

I recognise the flaws in my argument about demolishing the stadium, or part of it, and the emotions it provokes on all sides so perhaps it’s just enough to say I’ll never feel the same about the stadium as I once did.

Division: League Two Opened: 1994 Capacity: 8,203

Sixfields is a soulless ground anyway but its issues have been compounded by redevelopment delays and questions about missing money

It is a soulless ground anyway but its issues have been compounded by redevelopment delays and questions about missing money.

It has the same kind of deracinated feel as so many of the new-build stadia pushed to the peripheries of towns. Its supporters deserve a lot better.

Division: League Two Opened: 1997 Capacity: 5,907

If you visit the Broadfield Stadium, I think you might doubt if Crawley are even in League Two

Not an awful lot to relish about the Broadfield Stadium, to be honest.

Decent fans, of course, just like at every club, but Crawley Town’s home is a bit of a modern monstrosity, next to a roundabout outside town on the A23.

If you visit the Broadfield Stadium, I think you might doubt if Crawley are even in League Two. I had fun when I visited because I was in the away end with Stockport fans but I’m not in any hurry to go back.

85. Coventry Building Society Arena, Coventry City

Division: Premier League Opened: 2005 Capacity: 32,609

Football at the CBS Arena feels like it is in an urban wasteland but it is football, nonetheless

When it was called the Ricoh Arena, I had no interest in visiting what is now the Coventry Building Society Arena because it felt like a symbol of the callous way in which fans of the club were being treated by SISU, the hedge fund that owned it at the time.

But SISU sold up in the end and I went along a few years back to see Coventry dismantle Wayne Rooney’s Birmingham City. Then, in the press room beneath the stadium, I watched as my colleague Neil Moxley got into a decent old-fashioned row with Rooney about his stewardship of the Blues.

The atmosphere inside the ground was lively enough, partly because the game was a derby of sorts, but it is a soulless stadium abutting the M6.

It is football in an urban wasteland but it is football, nonetheless, and Doug King, the new owner, has brought with him much better times.

84. JobServe Community Stadium, Colchester United

Division: League Two Opened: 2008 Capacity: 10,105

This stadium on a roundabout on the A12 in the middle of a retail park is rather a bleak place to watch football

The staff at the club are great, the stewards are friendly, there's plenty of parking, there's a Wendy's next door and the home fans, largely arranged in a stand behind one of the goals, make a superb first of creating an atmosphere.

But this stadium on a roundabout on the A12 in the middle of a retail park is still rather a bleak place to watch football.

It probably didn’t help that I went on a dank March night when a wispy fog lingered in the dim floodlight glare but there was something ethereally gloomy about the JobServe Community Stadium.

The empty corridors and the cavernous suites lent it a slight feel of the Overlook Hotel on the inside. On the outside, the four corners of the stadium are open, which makes for especially bitter nights in the winter.

Home is home and there was still plenty of drama and passion in Colchester’s 1-0 victory over Chesterfield – the match I saw – but it came despite the stadium, not because of it.

Division: League Two Opened: 1990 Capacity: 10,863

The Bescot Stadium was the first of the generation of identikit new-build arenas I went to and there is not, frankly, much to recommend it apart from the loyalty of the fans

The Bescot was the first of the generation of identikit new-build arenas I went to and there is not, frankly, much to recommend it apart from the loyalty of the fans.

It’s close to the M6 and it’s a seven-minute walk to Walsall station – so you can get away from it quickly, which some would say is a bonus.

82. Brick Community Stadium, Wigan Athletic

Division: League One Opened: 1999 Capacity: 25,133

The name changes are irrelevant to some but they betray a lack of care for the identity of a football club

I stood on the terraces at Springfield Park as a Stockport fan.

Once again, it will not come as a surprise to learn I preferred it to its successor, the JJB Stadium, which later became the DW Stadium and is now the Brick Community Stadium.

The name changes are irrelevant to some but they betray a lack of care for the identity of a football club.

There were some great days and nights there when Wigan were promoted to the Premier League and I remember, in particular, the heady feeling of watching Wigan’s first home game in the top flight, against Jose Mourinho’s Chelsea in 2005.

The limelight has moved away again now and Wigan are left with a stadium that is perfectly adequate and also perfectly unremarkable.

Division: League Two Opened: 2007 Capacity: 9,875

Abutted by a McDonald’s and a TK Maxx on the outer fringes of the town, it feels like a disembodied place, separated from its community, functional but uninspired

Gay Meadow, the former home of Shrewsbury Town, was one of the best grounds in our top four divisions.

It might have flooded now and again because of its position on the banks of the River Severn but it was a fine old ground and the tradition of a boatman taking to a coracle to fish wayward shots that cleared the roof of the stand out of the river was one of the most cherished peculiarities in our game.

The Croud Meadow is altogether more prosaic. Abutted by a McDonald’s and a TK Maxx on the outer fringes of the town, it feels like a disembodied place, separated from its community, functional but uninspired.

Division: League One Opened: 1998 Capacity: 24,376

I was persona non grata for a while at the Select Car Leasing Stadium when I took exception to Reading taking out two Chelsea goalkeepers in one match back in 2006

I was persona non grata for a while at the Select Car Leasing Stadium when I took exception to Reading taking out two Chelsea goalkeepers in one match back in 2006, when Steve Coppell and Wally Downes were in charge at the Madejski Stadium.

People called it the Mad Stad back then and I remember Neil Warnock telling me about being chased to his car outside the main entrance when he was manager of Sheffield United.

And Wally took a swing at me at a Football Writers’ Association dinner a couple of years later.

Anyway, I’ve made up with Stephen Hunt, who was one of the players involved in the tumult against Chelsea, and with Downes since then.

Even if the Mad Stad doesn’t have an awful lot of personality, I have only respect for the Reading fans who endured so much under the ownership of Dai Yongge and fought for their club.

Division: Championship Opened: 1997 Capacity: 32,956

Too many of the modern bowls have lost character because the fans just merge into one

Pride Park is the standard-bearer, sadly, for what is lacking in many of the new generation of English football stadia.

English football grounds should be about the North Bank and the Stretford End and the Kop and the Gallowgate End and the Shelf.

They’re supposed to be about defined areas that give a stadium character and personality and even rivalry among home fans about who sings loudest.

Too many of the modern bowls have lost that character because the fans just merge into one.

This is not a criticism of Derby County fans in any way. They still make plenty of noise inside their stadium but the place is not a patch on the Baseball Ground, which witnessed so many momentous days and nights.

Pride Park is bland and featureless, a symbol of its team’s current struggle for identity as it languishes near the foot of the Championship.

Division: Championship Opened: 2003 Capacity: 20,996

The Swansea.com Stadium lacks character but is a tight ground where the fans can still generate a rousing atmosphere if their team’s displays allow it

My in-laws used to live in Swansea and when I wasn’t out walking to Worm’s Head at Rhossili or enjoying the delights of Mumbles and the Wales Coast Path, I’d make the occasional pilgrimage to what was left of the Vetch Field.

I stood in the away end there with Manchester United fans in the early 80s but when I visited later in my life, the Vetch was locked up and derelict. If you peered through the gates, you could see small trees and shrubs growing on the pitch.

The Swansea.com Stadium lacks the same character, obviously, but it is a tight ground where the fans can still generate a rousing atmosphere if their team’s displays allow it.
